4.123.s:
nārada uvāca
gaṇeśapūjanākhyānaṃ purāṇeṣu ca durlabham .
śrutaṃ tadbrahmaṇo vaktrātsāmānyaṃ ca samāsataḥ .. 1 ..
4.123.d:
नारद उवाच
गणेशपूजनाख्यानं पुराणेषु च दुर्लभम् ।
श्रुतं तद्ब्रह्मणो वक्त्रात्सामान्यं च समासतः ॥ 1 ॥

4.123.s:
mahimānaṃ gaṇapateḥ sarvabūjyeśvarasya ca .
vyāsena śrotumicchāmi yogīndrāṇāṃ gurorguroḥ .. 2 ..
4.123.d:
महिमानं गणपतेः सर्वबूज्येश्वरस्य च ।
व्यासेन श्रोतुमिच्छामि योगीन्द्राणां गुरोर्गुरोः ॥ 2 ॥
4.123.m:
I wish to hear in detail the majesty of Gaṇapati, the lord who is to be worshipped by all,
the guru of the gurus of the lords of yogins.

4.123.s:
siddhāśrame mahāpūja trailokyasthaiḥ kṛtā purā .
rādhāmādhavayostatra punaḥ saṃmīlaraṃ purā .. 3 ..
4.123.d:
सिद्धाश्रमे महापूज त्रैलोक्यस्थैः कृता पुरा ।
राधामाधवयोस्तत्र पुनः संमीलरं पुरा ॥ 3 ॥
4.123.m:
At Siddhāśrama, a great worship was performed formerly by the dwellers of the three worlds;
there, in former times, took place the reunion of Rādhā and Mādhava.

4.123.s:
atīte varṣaśatake śrīdāmnaḥ śāpamokṣaṇe .
ādau cakāra pūjāṃ ca sā ca rādhā kathaṃ mune .. 4 ..
4.123.d:
अतीते वर्षशतके श्रीदाम्नः शापमोक्षणे ।
आदौ चकार पूजां च सा च राधा कथं मुने ॥ 4 ॥
4.123.m:
When a hundred years had elapsed, upon the release from Śrīdāman's curse,
how did she, Rādhā, perform the worship in the beginning, O sage,

4.123.s:
sthiteṣu ca surendreṣu brahmaviṣṇuśivādiṣu .
nāgendre ca sthite śeṣe nāgeṣu ca mahatsu ca .. 5 ..
4.123.d:
स्थितेषु च सुरेन्द्रेषु ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादिषु ।
नागेन्द्रे च स्थिते शेषे नागेषु च महत्सु च ॥ 5 ॥
4.123.m:
while the lords of the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others were present,
and while Śeṣa, the lord of serpents, and the great serpents were present,

4.123.s:
rājendreṣu ca bhūmau ca baliṣṭheṣvasureṣu ca .
gandharveṣu ca rakṣaḥsu cānyeṣu balavatsu ca .. 6 ..
4.123.d:
राजेन्द्रेषु च भूमौ च बलिष्ठेष्वसुरेषु च ।
गन्धर्वेषु च रक्षःसु चान्येषु बलवत्सु च ॥ 6 ॥
4.123.m:
and the supreme kings on earth, the mighty asuras,
the gandharvas, the rakṣases, and other powerful beings?

4.123.s: vistareṇa mahābhāga tanme vyākhyātumarhasi .. 7 ..
4.123.d: विस्तरेण महाभाग तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥ 7 ॥
4.123.m: You ought to explain that to me in detail, O highly fortunate one.

4.123.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca
trelokye pṛthivī dhanyā mānyā puṇyavatī satī .
tatra bhāratavarṣaṃ ca karmaṇāṃ phaladaṃ śubham .. 8 ..
4.123.d:
नारायण उवाच
त्रेलोक्ये पृथिवी धन्या मान्या पुण्यवती सती ।
तत्र भारतवर्षं च कर्मणां फलदं शुभम् ॥ 8 ॥

4.123.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyaṃ pūjyaṃ ca puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate .
siddhāśramaṃ mahāpuṇyakṣetraṃ mokṣapradaṃ śubham .. 9 ..
4.123.d:
धन्यं यशस्यं पूज्यं च पुण्यक्षेत्रे च भारते ।
सिद्धाश्रमं महापुण्यक्षेत्रं मोक्षप्रदं शुभम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.123.m:
In the sacred land of Bhārata, blessed, famous, and venerable
is Siddhāśrama, a greatly meritorious sacred place, auspicious and bestowing liberation.

4.123.s:
sanatkumāro bhagavāṃstatra siddho babhūva ha .
svayaṃ vidhātā tatraiva taptvā siddho babhūva ha .. 10 ..
4.123.d:
सनत्कुमारो भगवांस्तत्र सिद्धो बभूव ह ।
स्वयं विधाता तत्रैव तप्त्वा सिद्धो बभूव ह ॥ 10 ॥
4.123.m: The blessed Sanatkumāra attained perfection there. / The Creator himself, having practiced austerities there, attained perfection. (10)

4.123.s:
yogīndrāśca munīndrāśca siddhendrāḥ kapilādayaḥ .
śatakrantūnmahendraśca tatra kṛtvā babhūva ha .. 11 ..
4.123.d:
योगीन्द्राश्च मुनीन्द्राश्च सिद्धेन्द्राः कपिलादयः ।
शतक्रन्तून्महेन्द्रश्च तत्र कृत्वा बभूव ह ॥ 11 ॥
4.123.m: Lords of yoga, lords of sages, and lords among the perfected, such as Kapila, [did so as well]. / And Mahendra, having performed a hundred sacrifices there, achieved his rank. (11)

4.123.s:
tena siddhāśramaṃ nāma sarveṣāmapi durlabham .
adhiṣṭhānaṃ gaṇeśasya tatreva satataṃ mune .. 12 ..
4.123.d:
तेन सिद्धाश्रमं नाम सर्वेषामपि दुर्लभम् ।
अधिष्ठानं गणेशस्य तत्रेव सततं मुने ॥ 12 ॥
4.123.m: Therefore it is named Siddhāśrama, difficult for all to attain. / O sage, it is the constant dwelling place of Gaṇeśa. (12)

4.123.s:
amūlyaratnanirmāṇagaṇeśapratimāṃ śubhām .
vaiśākhyāṃ pūrṇimāyāṃ ca pūjāṃ kurvanti devatāḥ .. 13 ..
4.123.d:
अमूल्यरत्ननिर्माणगणेशप्रतिमां शुभाम् ।
वैशाख्यां पूर्णिमायां च पूजां कुर्वन्ति देवताः ॥ 13 ॥
4.123.m: To the auspicious image of Gaṇeśa fashioned from priceless jewels, / the gods offer worship on the full moon day of the month of Vaiśākha. (13)

4.123.s:
nāgāśca mānavāścaiva daityā gandharvarākṣasāḥ .
siddhendrāśca munīndrāśca yogīndrāḥ sanakādayāḥ .. 14 ..
4.123.d:
नागाश्च मानवाश्चैव दैत्या गन्धर्वराक्षसाः ।
सिद्धेन्द्राश्च मुनीन्द्राश्च योगीन्द्राः सनकादयाः ॥ 14 ॥
4.123.m: Nāgas, human beings, daityas, gandharvas, rākṣasas, / lords among the perfected, lords among sages, and lords of yoga such as Sanaka and his brothers, (14)

4.123.s:
tatrā''jagāma śaṃbhuśca pārvatvā saha śaṃkaraḥ .
sagaṇaḥ kārtikeyaśca svayaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ .. 15 ..
4.123.d:
तत्रा'ऽजगाम शंभुश्च पार्वत्वा सह शंकरः ।
सगणः कार्तिकेयश्च स्वयं ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः ॥ 15 ॥
4.123.m: Śambhu came there, Śaṅkara along with Pārvatī, / attended by his host, and Kārtikeya, as well as Brahmā the Prajāpati himself. (15)

4.123.s:
tatrā''jagāma śeṣaśca nāgendraiḥ saha satvaram .
tajñā''jagmuḥ surāḥ sarve manavo mṛnayastathā .. 16 ..
4.123.d:
तत्रा'ऽजगाम शेषश्च नागेन्द्रैः सह सत्वरम् ।
तज्ञा'ऽजग्मुः सुराः सर्वे मनवो मृनयस्तथा ॥ 16 ॥
4.123.m: Śeṣa came there swiftly along with the chief serpents; / all the gods, Manus, and sages, wise in knowledge, came there. (16)

4.123.s:
ājagmuste nṛpāḥ sarve pūjārthaṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ .
āyayau bhagavānkṛṣṇo dvārakāvāsibhiḥ saha .. 17 ..
4.123.d:
आजग्मुस्ते नृपाः सर्वे पूजार्थं हृष्टमानसाः ।
आययौ भगवान्कृष्णो द्वारकावासिभिः सह ॥ 17 ॥
4.123.m: All those kings arrived, joyful in mind, for the sake of worship. / The blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa arrived along with the inhabitants of Dvārakā. (17)

4.123.s:
ājagāma tathā nandaḥ sārdhaṃ gokulavāsibhiḥ .
gopītriśatakoṭībhirgolokavāsibhiḥ saha .. 18 ..
4.123.d:
आजगाम तथा नन्दः सार्धं गोकुलवासिभिः ।
गोपीत्रिशतकोटीभिर्गोलोकवासिभिः सह ॥ 18 ॥
4.123.m: Likewise Nanda arrived together with the dwellers of Gokula, / along with three hundred crore gopīs, dwellers of Goloka. (18)

4.123.s:
gacendrakoṭitulyābhirbaliṣṭhābhiḥ sahā''libhiḥ .
āyayau sundarī rādhā kṛṣṇaprāṇādhidevatā .. 19 ..
4.123.d:
गचेन्द्रकोटितुल्याभिर्बलिष्ठाभिः सहा'ऽलिभिः ।
आययौ सुन्दरी राधा कृष्णप्राणाधिदेवता ॥ 19 ॥
4.123.m: Accompanied by mighty female companions equal to a crore of lordly elephants, / beautiful Rādhā, the presiding deity of Kṛṣṇa's life-breath, arrived. (19)

4.123.s:
rāseśvarī surasikā śatavarṣe gate sati .
susnātā mudatī śuddhā dhṛtvā dhaute ca vāsasī .. 20 ..
4.123.d:
रासेश्वरी सुरसिका शतवर्षे गते सति ।
सुस्नाता मुदती शुद्धा धृत्वा धौते च वाससी ॥ 20 ॥
4.123.m: The queen of the rāsa-dance, deeply appreciative of delight, after a hundred years had passed, / bathed well, joyful and pure, having put on two washed garments, (20)

4.123.s:
saṃyatā sā nirāhārā gatvā ca maṇimaṇḍapam .
suprakṣālitapādābjā kāntā bhuvanapāvanī .. 21 ..
4.123.d:
संयता सा निराहारा गत्वा च मणिमण्डपम् ।
सुप्रक्षालितपादाब्जा कान्ता भुवनपावनी ॥ 21 ॥
4.123.m: restrained and fasting, went to the jeweled pavilion; / her lotus feet thoroughly washed, the lovely one who purifies the worlds, (21)

4.123.s:
śrīkṛṣṇaprītikāmā'tha susaṃkalpaṃ vidhāya ca .
gaṅgodakena herambaṃ snāpayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ .. 22 ..
4.123.d:
श्रीकृष्णप्रीतिकामाऽथ सुसंकल्पं विधाय च ।
गङ्गोदकेन हेरम्बं स्नापयामास भक्तितः ॥ 22 ॥
4.123.m: desiring to please Śrī Kṛṣṇa, made an auspicious solemn resolve / and bathed Heramba with devotion using Gaṅgā water. (22)

4.123.s:
dhyārna ca sāmavedoktaṃ cakāra śuklapuṣpataḥ .
mātā caturṇāṃ vedānāṃ vasośca jagatāmapi .. 23 ..
4.123.d:
ध्यार्न च सामवेदोक्तं चकार शुक्लपुष्पतः ।
माता चतुर्णां वेदानां वसोश्च जगतामपि ॥ 23 ॥
4.123.m: She performed the meditation spoken in the Sāmaveda with a white flower— / the mother of the four Vedas, of the earth, and of the worlds, (23)

4.123.s:
buddhirūpā bhagavatī jñānināṃ jananī parā .
dhyānātmakaṃ svapusraṃ taṃ paraṃ dhyānaṃ cakāra sā .. 24 ..
4.123.d:
बुद्धिरूपा भगवती ज्ञानिनां जननी परा ।
ध्यानात्मकं स्वपुस्रं तं परं ध्यानं चकार सा ॥ 24 ॥
4.123.m: the goddess who is intellect itself, the supreme mother of the wise; / she performed the supreme meditation upon him whose nature is meditation, who is her own son: (24)

4.123.s:
śarvaṃ lambodaraṃ sthūlaṃ jvalantaṃ brahmatejasā .
gajavaktraṃ vahnivarṇamekadantamanantakam .. 25 ..
4.123.d:
शर्वं लम्बोदरं स्थूलं ज्वलन्तं ब्रह्मतेजसा ।
गजवक्त्रं वह्निवर्णमेकदन्तमनन्तकम् ॥ 25 ॥
4.123.m: “Śarva, pot-bellied, stout, blazing with the splendour of Brahman, / elephant-faced, fire-coloured, single-tusked, endless, (25)

4.123.s:
siddhānāṃ yogināmeva jñānināṃ ca gurorgurum .
dhyātaṃ munīndrairdevendrairbrahmeśaśeṣasaṃjñakaiḥ .. 26 ..
4.123.d:
सिद्धानां योगिनामेव ज्ञानिनां च गुरोर्गुरुम् ।
ध्यातं मुनीन्द्रैर्देवेन्द्रैर्ब्रह्मेशशेषसंज्ञकैः ॥ 26 ॥
4.123.m: the guru of gurus of the perfected, the yogins, and the wise, / meditated upon by the lords of sages, the lords of gods, and those known as Brahmā, Īśa, and Śeṣa, (26)

4.123.s:
siddhendrairmunibhiḥ sadbhirbhagavantaṃ sanātanam .
brahmasvarūpaṃ paramaṃ maṅgalaṃ maṅgalālayam .. 27 ..
4.123.d:
सिद्धेन्द्रैर्मुनिभिः सद्भिर्भगवन्तं सनातनम् ।
ब्रह्मस्वरूपं परमं मङ्गलं मङ्गलालयम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.123.m: by lords among the perfected, by virtuous sages—the eternal Lord, / whose own nature is Brahman, the supreme blessing, the abode of auspiciousness, (27)

4.123.s:
sarvavighnaharaṃ śāntaṃ dātāraṃ sarvasaṃpadām .
bhavābdhimāyāpotena karṇadhāraṃ ca karmiṇām .. 28 ..
4.123.d:
सर्वविघ्नहरं शान्तं दातारं सर्वसंपदाम् ।
भवाब्धिमायापोतेन कर्णधारं च कर्मिणाम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.123.m: the remover of all obstacles, peaceful, the bestower of all prosperity, / the helmsman for men of action using the boat across the ocean of worldly existence and delusion, (28)

4.123.s:
śaraṇāgatadīnārtaparitrāṇaparāyaṇam .
dhyāyeddhyānātmakaṃ sādhyaṃ bhakteśaṃ bhaktavatsalam .. 29 ..
4.123.d:
शरणागतदीनार्तपरित्राणपरायणम् ।
ध्यायेद्ध्यानात्मकं साध्यं भक्तेशं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.123.m: devoted to protecting the distressed and helpless who take refuge in him; / one should meditate on the one whose nature is meditation, who is to be attained, the lord of devotees, affectionate to his devotees.” (29)

4.123.s:
iti dhyātvā svaśirasi dattvā puṣpaṃ punaḥ satī .
sarvāṅgaśodhanaṃ nyāsaṃ vedoktaṃ ca cakāra sā .. 30 ..
4.123.d:
इति ध्यात्वा स्वशिरसि दत्त्वा पुष्पं पुनः सती ।
सर्वाङ्गशोधनं न्यासं वेदोक्तं च चकार सा ॥ 30 ॥
4.123.m: Having thus meditated and placed a flower upon her own head, the virtuous woman again / performed the ritual placement of mantras purifying all the limbs, as prescribed in the Vedas. (30)

4.123.s:
punaśca dhyātvā dhyānena tenaiva śubhadāyinā .
dadau puṣpaṃ pādapadme rādhā lambodarasya ca .. 31 ..
4.123.d:
पुनश्च ध्यात्वा ध्यानेन तेनैव शुभदायिना ।
ददौ पुष्पं पादपद्मे राधा लम्बोदरस्य च ॥ 31 ॥
4.123.m: Having meditated again with that very auspicious meditation, / Rādhā offered a flower at the lotus feet of the pot-bellied one. (31)

4.123.s:
saptatīrthodakenaiva śītena vāsitena ca .
dadau pādyaṃ pādapadme taiḥ padmādibhirarcite .. 32 ..
4.123.d:
सप्ततीर्थोदकेनैव शीतेन वासितेन च ।
ददौ पाद्यं पादपद्मे तैः पद्मादिभिरर्चिते ॥ 32 ॥
4.123.m: With water from the seven sacred places, cool and fragrant, / she gave water for the feet at his lotus feet worshipped by Padmā and others. (32)

4.123.s:
dūrvākṣataiḥ śuklapuṣpaiḥ sugandhicandanodakaiḥ .
arghyaṃ dadau tacchirasi svayaṃ golokavāsinī .. 33 ..
4.123.d:
दूर्वाक्षतैः शुक्लपुष्पैः सुगन्धिचन्दनोदकैः ।
अर्घ्यं ददौ तच्छिरसि स्वयं गोलोकवासिनी ॥ 33 ॥
4.123.m: With dūrvā grass, unbroken grain, white flowers, and fragrant sandalwood-water, / she who dwells in Goloka herself offered the guest-offering on his head. (33)

4.123.s:
sacandanaṃ sgdhimālyaṃ pārijātasya sundaram .
dadau gale gaṇeśasya svayaṃ rāsaṃśvarī mudā .. 34 ..
4.123.d:
सचन्दनं स्ग्धिमाल्यं पारिजातस्य सुन्दरम् ।
ददौ गले गणेशस्य स्वयं रासंश्वरी मुदा ॥ 34 ॥
4.123.m: With joy, the queen of the rāsa-dance herself placed a beautiful fragrant garland / of pārijāta flowers smeared with sandalwood upon the neck of Gaṇeśa. (34)

4.123.s:
kastūrīkuṅkumāktaṃ ca sugandhi snigdhacandanam .
sarvāṅge pradadau tasya vṛndāvanavinodinī .. 35 ..
4.123.d:
कस्तूरीकुङ्कुमाक्तं च सुगन्धि स्निग्धचन्दनम् ।
सर्वाङ्गे प्रददौ तस्य वृन्दावनविनोदिनी ॥ 35 ॥
4.123.m: She who delights in Vṛndāvana applied fragrant, smooth sandalwood / mixed with musk and saffron over all his limbs. (35)

4.123.s:
sugandhi śuklaṃ puṣpaṃ ca sugandha candanārcitam .
dadau tasya padāmbhoje mahāpadmalayā satī .. 36 ..
4.123.d:
सुगन्धि शुक्लं पुष्पं च सुगन्ध चन्दनार्चितम् ।
ददौ तस्य पदाम्भोजे महापद्मलया सती ॥ 36 ॥
4.123.m: The virtuous lady whose abode is the great lotus / offered a fragrant white flower worshipped with sweet-smelling sandalwood at his lotus feet. (36)

4.123.s:
sugandhiyuktaṃ dhūpaṃ ca pūtairvastubhiranvitam .
dadau kṛṣṇapriyā tasmai jagatāmīśvarāya ca .. 37 ..
4.123.d:
सुगन्धियुक्तं धूपं च पूतैर्वस्तुभिरन्वितम् ।
ददौ कृष्णप्रिया तस्मै जगतामीश्वराय च ॥ 37 ॥
4.123.m: Kṛṣṇa's beloved offered sweet-scented incense / composed of pure substances to him, the Lord of the worlds. (37)

4.123.s:
dīpaṃ ghṛtapradīptaṃ ca dhvāntavidhvaṃsakāraṇam .
dadau tasmai sureśāya paramādyā sanātanī .. 38 ..
4.123.d:
दीपं घृतप्रदीप्तं च ध्वान्तविध्वंसकारणम् ।
ददौ तस्मै सुरेशाय परमाद्या सनातनी ॥ 38 ॥
4.123.m: The primordial, eternal goddess offered a lamp, / blazing with clarified butter and destroying darkness, to him, the lord of the gods. (38)

4.123.s:
naivedya vividhaṃ ramyaṃ susvādu sumanoharam .
coṣyaṃ carvyaṃ lehyapeye sudhātulyaṃ caturvidham .. 39 ..
4.123.d:
नैवेद्य विविधं रम्यं सुस्वादु सुमनोहरम् ।
चोष्यं चर्व्यं लेह्यपेये सुधातुल्यं चतुर्विधम् ॥ 39 ॥
4.123.m: Various, delightful, very tasty, and charming food offerings— / the four types: food to be sucked, chewed, licked, and drunk, equal to nectar, (39)

4.123.s:
phalāni ca supakvāni trailokye durlabhāni ca .
madhurāṇi ca mūlāni grāmyāraṇyāni nārada .. 40 ..
4.123.d:
फलानि च सुपक्वानि त्रैलोक्ये दुर्लभानि च ।
मधुराणि च मूलानि ग्राम्यारण्यानि नारद ॥ 40 ॥
4.123.m: and fully ripened fruits rare in the three worlds, / and sweet roots, cultivated and wild, O Nārada, (40)

4.123.s:
tāni tvanyānyasaṃkhyāni tilānāṃ laḍḍukāni ca .
laḍḍukāni supakvāni svādūni surasāni ca .. 41 ..
4.123.d:
तानि त्वन्यान्यसंख्यानि तिलानां लड्डुकानि च ।
लड्डुकानि सुपक्वानि स्वादूनि सुरसानि च ॥ 41 ॥
4.123.m: and countless other laddu sweets made of sesame seeds, / laddus well-cooked, tasty, and delicious, (41)

4.123.s:
yavagodhūmacūrṇānāṃ pakvāni piṣṭakāni ca .
ghṛtāktāni ca ramyāṇi śarkarāsahitāni ca .. 42 ..
4.123.d:
यवगोधूमचूर्णानां पक्वानि पिष्टकानि च ।
घृताक्तानि च रम्याणि शर्करासहितानि च ॥ 42 ॥
4.123.m: cooked cakes of barley and wheat flour, / smeared with clarified butter, delightful, and served with sugar, (42)

4.123.s:
svāstikānāṃ laḍḍukāni sthūlāni sundarāṇi ca .
bhṛṣṭadravyaṃ ca vividhamakṣataṃ śarkarānvitam .. 43 ..
4.123.d:
स्वास्तिकानां लड्डुकानि स्थूलानि सुन्दराणि च ।
भृष्टद्रव्यं च विविधमक्षतं शर्करान्वितम् ॥ 43 ॥
4.123.m: large and handsome laddus shaped as svastikas, / and various parched grains along with unbroken rice and sugar, (43)

4.123.s:
ghṛtakulyāṃ dugdhakulayāṃ madhukulyaṃ manoharām .
guḍasya dadhnaḥ kulyāṃ ca pāyasānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 44 ..
4.123.d:
घृतकुल्यां दुग्धकुलयां मधुकुल्यं मनोहराम् ।
गुडस्य दध्नः कुल्यां च पायसानां तथैव च ॥ 44 ॥
4.123.m: a stream of clarified butter, a stream of milk, a charming stream of honey, / a stream of molasses, of curd, and likewise of milk-rice, (44)

4.123.s:
piṣṭakānāṃ svastikānāṃ rambhāṇāṃ rāśireva ca .
miṣṭavyañjanayuktāni śālyannāni śubhāni ca .. 45 ..
4.123.d:
पिष्टकानां स्वस्तिकानां रम्भाणां राशिरेव च ।
मिष्टव्यञ्जनयुक्तानि शाल्यन्नानि शुभानि च ॥ 45 ॥
4.123.m: a heap of cakes, svastika pastries, and plantains, / and pure rice of winter grain accompanied by sweet vegetables (45)

4.123.s:
dadau tasmai sureśāya kṛṣṇaprāṇādhidevatā .
amūlyaratnanirmāṇaṃ ramyaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ varam .. 46 ..
4.123.d:
ददौ तस्मै सुरेशाय कृष्णप्राणाधिदेवता ।
अमूल्यरत्ननिर्माणं रम्यं सिंहासनं वरम् ॥ 46 ॥
4.123.m: the presiding deity of Kṛṣṇa's life-breath offered to that lord of the gods. / An excellent, charming throne fashioned of priceless jewels (46)

4.123.s:
dadau vighnapināśāya virājataṭavāsinī .
sūkṣmavastrayugaṃ ramyamamūlyaṃ vahniśuddhakam .. 47 ..
4.123.d:
ददौ विघ्नपिनाशाय विराजतटवासिनी ।
सूक्ष्मवस्त्रयुगं रम्यममूल्यं वह्निशुद्धकम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.123.m: she who dwells on the bank of the Virajā river gave to the destroyer of obstacles, / as well as a charming pair of fine garments, priceless and purified by fire. (47)

4.123.s:
dadau śailātmajāyaiva śataśṛṅganivāsinī .
viśuddhasarpiṣā yuktaṃ nirmalaṃ madhuraṃ madhu .. 48 ..
4.123.d:
ददौ शैलात्मजायैव शतशृङ्गनिवासिनी ।
विशुद्धसर्पिषा युक्तं निर्मलं मधुरं मधु ॥ 48 ॥
4.123.m: She who dwells on Śataśṛṅga gave to the son of the mountain's daughter / pure, sweet honey mixed with pure clarified butter. (48)

4.123.s:
madhuparkaṃ dadau tasmai vṛndāvananivāsinī .
tāmbūlaṃ ca varaṃ ramyaṃ karpūrādisuvāsitam .. 49 ..
4.123.d:
मधुपर्कं ददौ तस्मै वृन्दावननिवासिनी ।
ताम्बूलं च वरं रम्यं कर्पूरादिसुवासितम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.123.m: She who dwells in Vṛndāvana offered him the honey-mixture; / and an excellent, charming betel preparation fragrant with camphor and other spices (49)

4.123.s:
sarvasaṃpatpradātre ca vṛṣabhānasutā dadau .
saptatīrthodakaṃ śuddhaṃ susitaṃ suvāsitam .. 50 ..
4.123.d:
सर्वसंपत्प्रदात्रे च वृषभानसुता ददौ ।
सप्ततीर्थोदकं शुद्धं सुसितं सुवासितम् ॥ 50 ॥
4.123.m: the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu gave to the bestower of all prosperity; / pure water from the seven sacred places, very cool and fragrant, (50)

4.123.s:
pānārtha ca jalaṃ tasmai dadau gaupośvarī mudā .
amūlyaṃ durlabhaṃ caiva viśuddhaṃ śvetacāmaram .. 51 ..
4.123.d:
पानार्थ च जलं तस्मै ददौ गौपोश्वरी मुदा ।
अमूल्यं दुर्लभं चैव विशुद्धं श्वेतचामरम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.123.m: water for drinking she, the queen of the cowherds, joyfully gave to him; / a priceless and rare, spotless white fly-whisk (51)

4.123.s:
dadau tasmai pareśāya mūlaprakṛtirīśvarī .
amūlyaratnanirmāṇaṃ muktāmāṇikyahīrakaiḥ .. 52 ..
4.123.d:
ददौ तस्मै परेशाय मूलप्रकृतिरीश्वरी ।
अमूल्यरत्ननिर्माणं मुक्तामाणिक्यहीरकैः ॥ 52 ॥
4.123.m: the sovereign lady, Primordial Nature, offered to the supreme lord; / and a fine bedstead fashioned with priceless gems, (52)

4.123.s:
pariṣkṛtaṃ sutalpaṃ ca puṣpacandanacarcitam .
sitasūkṣmāśukenaiva paritaśca pariṣkṛtam .. 53 ..
4.123.d:
परिष्कृतं सुतल्पं च पुष्पचन्दनचर्चितम् ।
सितसूक्ष्माशुकेनैव परितश्च परिष्कृतम् ॥ 53 ॥
4.123.m: adorned with pearls, rubies, and diamonds, smeared with flowers and sandalwood, / and decorated all around with fine white cloth, (53)

4.123.s:
dadau śivātmajāyaiva kṛṣṇavakṣaḥsthalasthitā .
dattvā ca kāmadhenuṃ ca savatsāṃ vāñchitapradām .. 54 ..
4.123.d:
ददौ शिवात्मजायैव कृष्णवक्षःस्थलस्थिता ।
दत्त्वा च कामधेनुं च सवत्सां वाञ्छितप्रदाम् ॥ 54 ॥
4.123.m: she who dwells upon Kṛṣṇa's chest gave to the son of Śiva. / And having given the wish-yielding cow along with her calf, which grants desired wishes, (54)

4.123.s:
kṛtvā'tīva parīhāraṃ vṛndā puṣpāñjaliṃ dadau .
divyena mūlmanunā sabījenojjvalena ca .. 55 ..
4.123.d:
कृत्वाऽतीव परीहारं वृन्दा पुष्पाञ्जलिं ददौ ।
दिव्येन मूल्मनुना सबीजेनोज्ज्वलेन च ॥ 55 ॥
4.123.m: Offering the deepest humbleness, Vṛndā presented a handful of flowers / with the divine root-mantra, accompanied by its seed-syllable and radiant.

4.123.s:
dadau ṣoḍaśopacāraṃ kālindīkulavāsinī .
oṃ gaṃ gauṃ gaṇapataye vighnavināśine svāhā .. 56 ..
4.123.d:
ददौ षोडशोपचारं कालिन्दीकुलवासिनी ।
ओं गं गौं गणपतये विघ्नविनाशिने स्वाहा ॥ 56 ॥
4.123.m: The dweller on the banks of the Kālindī offered the sixteen articles of worship: / 'Om gam gaum to Gaṇapati, the destroyer of obstacles, svāhā.'

4.123.s:
ityevameva mantraṃ ca gāṇeśaṃ ṣoḍaśākṣaram .
sā jajāpa sahasraṃ ca paraṃ salpataruṃ varam .. 57 ..
4.123.d:
इत्येवमेव मन्त्रं च गाणेशं षोडशाक्षरम् ।
सा जजाप सहस्रं च परं सल्पतरुं वरम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.123.m: Reciting precisely this sixteen-syllable mantra dedicated to Gaṇeśa, / she chanted it a thousand times, that supreme, excellent wish-yielding tree.

4.123.s:
tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharā .
sāśrunetrā pulakitā stotreṇa kauthumena ca .. 58 ..
4.123.d:
तुष्टाव परया भक्त्या भक्तिनम्रात्मकंधरा ।
साश्रुनेत्रा पुलकिता स्तोत्रेण कौथुमेन च ॥ 58 ॥
4.123.m: With supreme devotion, bowing her neck in submission, / with tearful eyes and bristling with joy, she praised him with the Kauthuma hymn of praise.

4.123.s:
rādhikovāca
paraṃ dhāma paraṃ brahma pareśaṃ parameśvaram .
vighnanighnakaraṃ śāntaṃ puṣṭaṃ kāntamanantakam .. 59 ..
4.123.d:
राधिकोवाच
परं धाम परं ब्रह्म परेशं परमेश्वरम् ।
विघ्ननिघ्नकरं शान्तं पुष्टं कान्तमनन्तकम् ॥ 59 ॥
4.123.m: Rādhikā said: / The supreme abode, the supreme Brahman, the lord of the highest, the supreme Lord, / who destroys obstacles, calm, flourishing, beautiful, infinite;

4.123.s:
surāsurendraiḥ siddhendraiḥ stutaṃ staumi parātparam .
surapadmadineśaṃ ca gaṇeśaṃ maṅgalāyanam .. 60 ..
4.123.d:
सुरासुरेन्द्रैः सिद्धेन्द्रैः स्तुतं स्तौमि परात्परम् ।
सुरपद्मदिनेशं च गणेशं मङ्गलायनम् ॥ 60 ॥
4.123.m: Praised by the lords of gods and asuras, and by the lords of siddhas, I praise that one who is beyond the highest, / the sun to the lotuses that are the gods, Gaṇeśa, the abode of auspiciousness.

4.123.s:
idaṃ stotraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ vighnaśokaharaṃ param .
yaḥ paṭhetprātarutthāya sarvavighnātpramucyate .. 61 ..
4.123.d:
इदं स्तोत्रं महापुण्यं विघ्नशोकहरं परम् ।
यः पठेत्प्रातरुत्थाय सर्वविघ्नात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 61 ॥
4.123.m: This hymn of praise is exceedingly meritorious, the supreme dispeller of obstacles and grief. / Whoever recites it upon rising at dawn is liberated from every obstacle.

4.123.s:
iti śrībrahmao mahāo śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhao uttao nāradanāo trayoviṃśatya-
dhikaśatatamo'dhyoyaḥ .. 123 ..
4.123.d:
इति श्रीब्रह्मओ महाओ श्रीकृष्णजन्मखओ उत्तओ नारदनाओ त्रयोविंशत्य-
धिकशततमोऽध्योयः ॥ 123 ॥
4.123.m: Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-third chapter in the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa, second part, of the glorious and great Brahmavaivarta, [in the dialogue between] Nārada and Nārāyaṇa. 123.

4.124.s:
atha caturviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo'dhyoyaḥ
nālāyaṇa uvāca
rādhā saṃpūjya vidhinā stutvā lambodaraṃ satī .
amūlyaratnanirmāṇaṃ sarvāṅgabhūṣaṇaṃ dadau .. 1 ..
4.124.d:
अथ चतुर्विंशत्यधिकशततमोऽध्योयः
नालायण उवाच
राधा संपूज्य विधिना स्तुत्वा लम्बोदरं सती ।
अमूल्यरत्ननिर्माणं सर्वाङ्गभूषणं ददौ ॥ 1 ॥
4.124.m: Now begins the one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter. / Nārāyaṇa said: / Having worshipped Lambodara according to the rites and praised him, the chaste Rādhā / offered ornaments for all his limbs crafted of priceless gems.

4.124.s:
rādhāyāḥ stavanaṃ śrutvā pūjāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca vastu ca .
uvāca madhuraṃ śāntaḥ śāntāṃ trailokyamātaram .. 2 ..
4.124.d:
राधायाः स्तवनं श्रुत्वा पूजां दृष्ट्वा च वस्तु च ।
उवाच मधुरं शान्तः शान्तां त्रैलोक्यमातरम् ॥ 2 ॥
4.124.m: Hearing Rādhā's praise and seeing the worship and the offerings, / the tranquil one spoke sweetly to the tranquil mother of the three worlds.

4.124.s:
gaṇeśa uvāca
tava pūjā jaganmātarlokaśikṣākarī śubhe .
brahmasvarūpā bhavatī kṛṣṇavakṣaḥ sthalasthitā .. 3 ..
4.124.d:
गणेश उवाच
तव पूजा जगन्मातर्लोकशिक्षाकरी शुभे ।
ब्रह्मस्वरूपा भवती कृष्णवक्षः स्थलस्थिता ॥ 3 ॥
4.124.m: Gaṇeśa said: / O Mother of the universe, O auspicious one, your worship is meant to instruct the world. / You are of the nature of Brahman, resting upon the chest of Kṛṣṇa.

4.124.s:
yatpādapadmatulaṃ dhyāyante te sudurlabham .
surā brahmeśaśeṣādyā munīndrāḥ sanakādayaḥ .. 4 ..
4.124.d:
यत्पादपद्मतुलं ध्यायन्ते ते सुदुर्लभम् ।
सुरा ब्रह्मेशशेषाद्या मुनीन्द्राः सनकादयः ॥ 4 ॥
4.124.m: The gods headed by Brahmā, Śiva, and Śeṣa, the best of munis headed by Sanaka, / whose matchless lotus feet they meditate upon, so hard to attain,

4.124.s:
jīvanmuktāśca bhaktāśca siddhendrāḥ kapilādayaḥ .
tasya prāṇādhidevī tvaṃ priyā prāṇādhikā parā .. 5 ..
4.124.d:
जीवन्मुक्ताश्च भक्ताश्च सिद्धेन्द्राः कपिलादयः ।
तस्य प्राणाधिदेवी त्वं प्रिया प्राणाधिका परा ॥ 5 ॥
4.124.m: As well as those liberated while living, devotees, and lords of siddhas headed by Kapila; / you are the presiding deity of his life-breath, his supreme beloved, dearer than his own life.

4.124.s:
vāmāṅganirmitā rādhā dakṣiṇāṅgaśca mādhavaḥ .
mahālakṣmīrjaganmātā tava vāmāṅganirmitā .. 6 ..
4.124.d:
वामाङ्गनिर्मिता राधा दक्षिणाङ्गश्च माधवः ।
महालक्ष्मीर्जगन्माता तव वामाङ्गनिर्मिता ॥ 6 ॥
4.124.m: Rādhā was formed from his left side, and Mādhava is his right side; / Mahālakṣmī, mother of the universe, was formed from your left side.

4.124.s:
vasoḥ sarvanivāsasya prasūstvaṃ parameśvarī .
vedānāṃ jagatāmeva mūlprakṛtirīśvarī .. 7 ..
4.124.d:
वसोः सर्वनिवासस्य प्रसूस्त्वं परमेश्वरी ।
वेदानां जगतामेव मूल्प्रकृतिरीश्वरी ॥ 7 ॥
4.124.m: You are the supreme Goddess, the mother of the Vasu who is the abode of all, / the sovereign root Prakṛti of the Vedas and of the worlds.

4.124.s:
sarvāḥ prākṛtikā mātaḥ sṛṣṭyāṃ ca tvadvibhūtayaḥ .
viśvāni kāryarūpāṇi tvaṃ ca kāraṇarūpiṇī .. 8 ..
4.124.d:
सर्वाः प्राकृतिका मातः सृष्ट्यां च त्वद्विभूतयः ।
विश्वानि कार्यरूपाणि त्वं च कारणरूपिणी ॥ 8 ॥
4.124.m: All things born of Prakṛti in creation, O Mother, are your manifestations; / the cosmic realms are of the nature of effects, and you are of the nature of cause.

4.124.s:
pralaye brahmaṇaḥ pāte tannimeṣo harerapi .
ādau rādhāṃ samuccārya paścātkṛṣṇaṃ parātparam .. 9 ..
4.124.d:
प्रलये ब्रह्मणः पाते तन्निमेषो हरेरपि ।
आदौ राधां समुच्चार्य पश्चात्कृष्णं परात्परम् ॥ 9 ॥
4.124.m: At the cosmic dissolution, when Brahmā falls, that is but a blink of the eye for Hari. / Uttering 'Rādhā' first and thereafter 'Kṛṣṇa' who is beyond the highest,

4.124.s:
sa eva paṇḍito yogī golokaṃ yāti līlayā .
vyatikrame mahāpāpī brahmahatyāṃ labhetdhruvam.. 10 ..
4.124.d:
स एव पण्डितो योगी गोलोकं याति लीलया ।
व्यतिक्रमे महापापी ब्रह्महत्यां लभेत्ध्रुवम्॥ 10 ॥
4.124.m: He indeed is a wise yogin and effortlessly goes to Goloka; / in reversing the order, a great sinner surely incurs [the sin of] murdering a brāhmaṇa.

4.124.s:
jagatāṃ bhavatī mātā paramātmā pitā hariḥ .
pitureva gururmātā pūjyā vandyā parātparā .. 11 ..
4.124.d:
जगतां भवती माता परमात्मा पिता हरिः ।
पितुरेव गुरुर्माता पूज्या वन्द्या परात्परा ॥ 11 ॥
4.124.m: You are the mother of the worlds, and the Paramātman Hari is the father; / the mother is indeed a teacher higher than the father, worthy of worship, adoration, and beyond the highest.

4.124.s:
bhajate devamanyaṃ vā kṛṣṇaṃ vā sarvakāraṇam .
puṇyakṣetre mahāmūḍho yadi nindati rādhikām .. 12 ..
4.124.d:
भजते देवमन्यं वा कृष्णं वा सर्वकारणम् ।
पुण्यक्षेत्रे महामूढो यदि निन्दति राधिकाम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.124.m: Whether he worships another deity or Kṛṣṇa, the cause of all, / if in a sacred land a great fool insults Rādhikā,

4.124.s:
vaṃśahānirbhavettasya duḥkhaśokamihaiva ca .
pacyate niraye ghore yāvaccandradivākarau .. 13 ..
4.124.d:
वंशहानिर्भवेत्तस्य दुःखशोकमिहैव च ।
पच्यते निरये घोरे यावच्चन्द्रदिवाकरौ ॥ 13 ॥
4.124.m: The destruction of his lineage ensues, along with sorrow and grief in this very life, / and he cooks in a terrible hell as long as the moon and the sun endure.

4.124.s:
guruścajñānodgiraṇājjñānaṃ syānmantratantrayoḥ .
sa ca mantraśca tattantraṃ bhaktiḥ syāddhruvayoryataḥ .. 14 ..
4.124.d:
गुरुश्चज्ञानोद्गिरणाज्ज्ञानं स्यान्मन्त्रतन्त्रयोः ।
स च मन्त्रश्च तत्तन्त्रं भक्तिः स्याद्ध्रुवयोर्यतः ॥ 14 ॥
4.124.m: And the guru, by pouring forth knowledge, gives knowledge of mantra and tantra; / and that mantra and that tantra are those through which firm devotion to the two of you arises.

4.124.s:
niṣevya mantraṃ devānāṃ jīvā janmani janmani .
bhaktā bhavanti durgāyāḥ pādapadme sudurlabhe .. 15 ..
4.124.d:
निषेव्य मन्त्रं देवानां जीवा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
भक्ता भवन्ति दुर्गायाः पादपद्मे सुदुर्लभे ॥ 15 ॥
4.124.m: Serving the mantra of the gods birth after birth, / living beings become devotees at the lotus feet of Durgā, which are so hard to attain.

4.124.s:
niṣevya mantre śaṃbhośca jagatāṃ kāraṇasya ca .
tadā prāpnoti yuvayoḥ pādapadmaṃ sudurlabham .. 16 ..
4.124.d:
निषेव्य मन्त्रे शंभोश्च जगतां कारणस्य च ।
तदा प्राप्नोति युवयोः पादपद्मं सुदुर्लभम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.124.m: By serving the mantra of Śambhu, the cause of the worlds, / one then attains the very hard-to-attain lotus feet of you two.

4.124.s:
yukyoḥ pādapadmaṃ ca durlabhaṃ prāpya puṇyavān .
kṣaṇārdhaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ ca nahi muñcati daivataḥ .. 17 ..
4.124.d:
युक्योः पादपद्मं च दुर्लभं प्राप्य पुण्यवान् ।
क्षणार्धं षोडशांशं च नहि मुञ्चति दैवतः ॥ 17 ॥
4.124.m: Having attained the hard-to-attain lotus feet of you two, the meritorious one / does not let go by chance for half a moment or even a sixteenth of a part.

4.124.s:
bhaktyā ca yuvacormantraṃ gṛhītvā vaiṣmapādapi .
stavaṃ vā kavacaṃ vā'pi karmamūlanikṛntanam .. 18 ..
4.124.d:
भक्त्या च युवचोर्मन्त्रं गृहीत्वा वैष्मपादपि ।
स्तवं वा कवचं वाऽपि कर्ममूलनिकृन्तनम् ॥ 18 ॥
4.124.m: Receiving with devotion the mantra of you two, or a hymn of praise, or an armour, / from a Vaiṣṇava, which severs the root of karma,

4.124.s:
yojayetparayā bhaktyā puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate .
puruṣāṇāṃ sahasraṃ ca tvātmanā sārdhamuddharet .. 19 ..
4.124.d:
योजयेत्परया भक्त्या पुण्यक्षेत्रे च भारते ।
पुरुषाणां सहस्रं च त्वात्मना सार्धमुद्धरेत् ॥ 19 ॥
4.124.m: And applying it with supreme devotion in the sacred field of Bhārata, / he delivers a thousand generations along with himself.

4.124.s:
gurumabhyarcya vidhivadvastrālaṃkāracandanaiḥ .
kavacaṃ dhārayedyo hi viṣṇutulyo bhaveddhruvam .. 20 ..
4.124.d:
गुरुमभ्यर्च्य विधिवद्वस्त्रालंकारचन्दनैः ।
कवचं धारयेद्यो हि विष्णुतुल्यो भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 20 ॥
4.124.m: Having worshipped the guru according to the rites with garments, ornaments, and sandalwood paste, / whoever wears the armour surely becomes equal to Viṣṇu.

4.124.s:
yaddattaṃ vastu me mātastatsarvaṃ sārthakaṃ kuru .
dehi viprāya matprītyā tadā bhokṣyāmi sāṃpratam .. 21 ..
4.124.d:
यद्दत्तं वस्तु मे मातस्तत्सर्वं सार्थकं कुरु ।
देहि विप्राय मत्प्रीत्या तदा भोक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.124.m: Whatever articles have been given to me, O Mother, make them all fruitful: / give them to a brāhmaṇa for my satisfaction, and then I will partake of them now.

4.124.s:
deve deyāni dānāni deve deyā ca dakṣiṇā .
tatsarvaṃ brāhmaṇe dadyāttadānantyāya kalpate .. 22 ..
4.124.d:
देवे देयानि दानानि देवे देया च दक्षिणा ।
तत्सर्वं ब्राह्मणे दद्यात्तदानन्त्याय कल्पते ॥ 22 ॥
4.124.m: Gifts are to be given to a deity, and the sacrificial fee is to be given to a deity; / all that one should give to a brāhmaṇa, for then it produces infinite [fruit].

4.124.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ mukhaṃ rādhe devānāṃ mukhamukhyakam .
viprabhuktaṃ ca yaddravyaṃ prāpnuvantyeva devatāḥ .. 23 ..
4.124.d:
ब्राह्मणानां मुखं राधे देवानां मुखमुख्यकम् ।
विप्रभुक्तं च यद्द्रव्यं प्राप्नुवन्त्येव देवताः ॥ 23 ॥
4.124.m: The mouth of brāhmaṇas, O Rādhā, is the foremost mouth of the deities; / whatever substance is consumed by a brāhmaṇa, the deities indeed receive.

4.124.s:
viprāṃśca bhojayāmāsa tatsarva rādhikā satī .
babhūva tatkṣaṇādeva prīto lambodaro mune .. 24 ..
4.124.d:
विप्रांश्च भोजयामास तत्सर्व राधिका सती ।
बभूव तत्क्षणादेव प्रीतो लम्बोदरो मुने ॥ 24 ॥
4.124.m: The chaste Rādhikā fed all of that to the brāhmaṇas; / instantly Lambodara became pleased, O sage.

4.124.s:
etasminnantare devā brahmeśaśeṣasaṃjñakāḥ .
āyayurvaṭamūlaṃ ca devapūjārthameva ca .. 25 ..
4.124.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवा ब्रह्मेशशेषसंज्ञकाः ।
आययुर्वटमूलं च देवपूजार्थमेव च ॥ 25 ॥
4.124.m: In the meantime, the gods named Brahmā, Śiva, and Śeṣa / arrived at the root of the banyan tree for the purpose of worshipping the god.

4.124.s:
tatra gatvā śivacaro devāndevīruvāca saḥ .
śrīkṛṣṇaṃ śuṣkakaṇṭhaśca bhayabhītaśca rakṣakaḥ .. 26 ..
4.124.d:
तत्र गत्वा शिवचरो देवान्देवीरुवाच सः ।
श्रीकृष्णं शुष्ककण्ठश्च भयभीतश्च रक्षकः ॥ 26 ॥
4.124.m: Having gone there, that guard, a attendant of Śiva, / parched at the throat and terrified with fear, spoke to the gods and goddesses, and to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

4.124.s:
rakṣaka uvāca
gaṇeśaṃ pūjayāmāsa sarvādau ca śubhakṣaṇe .
vṛṣabhānasutā rādhā prakṛtya svastivācanam .. 27 ..
4.124.d:
रक्षक उवाच
गणेशं पूजयामास सर्वादौ च शुभक्षणे ।
वृषभानसुता राधा प्रकृत्य स्वस्तिवाचनम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.124.m: The guard said: / First of all, at the auspicious moment, Gaṇeśa was worshipped / by Rādhā, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, who performed the recitation of auspiciousness with Prakṛti,

4.124.s:
sahitā sā balavatī gopītriśatakoṭibhiḥ .
vārito'haṃ valiṣṭhābhiryuṣmāṃśca kathayāmi tat .. 28 ..
4.124.d:
सहिता सा बलवती गोपीत्रिशतकोटिभिः ।
वारितोऽहं वलिष्ठाभिर्युष्मांश्च कथयामि तत् ॥ 28 ॥
4.124.m: Accompanied by three hundred crores of powerful gopīs. / I was held back by those mighty women, and I tell you that.

4.124.s:
marvādau pūjayedyo hi so'nantaṃ phalamālabhet .
madhye madhyavidhaṃ puṇyaṃ śeṣe svalpamiti smṛtam .. 29 ..
4.124.d:
मर्वादौ पूजयेद्यो हि सोऽनन्तं फलमालभेत् ।
मध्ये मध्यविधं पुण्यं शेषे स्वल्पमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.124.m: Whoever worships first of all receives infinite reward; / in the middle [one receives] middling merit; at the end it is said to be very little.

4.124.s:
devendreṣu munīndreṣu devastrīṣu sthitāsu ca .
gopībhiśca saha tayā rādhayā pūjitaḥ paraḥ .. 30 ..
4.124.d:
देवेन्द्रेषु मुनीन्द्रेषु देवस्त्रीषु स्थितासु च ।
गोपीभिश्च सह तया राधया पूजितः परः ॥ 30 ॥
4.124.m: While the chiefs of gods, the lords of munis, and the celestial women were present, / that Supreme One was worshipped by that Rādhā along with the gopīs.

4.124.s:
dūtavākyaṃ samākarṇya jahasuḥ sarvadevatāḥ .
munayo manavaścaiva rājāno devayoṣitaḥ .. 31 ..
4.124.d:
दूतवाक्यं समाकर्ण्य जहसुः सर्वदेवताः ।
मुनयो मनवश्चैव राजानो देवयोषितः ॥ 31 ॥
4.124.m: Hearing the messenger's words, all the deities laughed, / as did the munis, the Manus, the kings, and the wives of the gods.

4.124.s:
rukmiṇyādyā ramaṇyaśca yā devyo vismayaṃ yayuḥ .
sarasvatī ca sāvitrī pārvatī parameśvarī .. 32 ..
4.124.d:
रुक्मिण्याद्या रमण्यश्च या देव्यो विस्मयं ययुः ।
सरस्वती च सावित्री पार्वती परमेश्वरी ॥ 32 ॥
4.124.m: The divine women headed by Rukmiṇī were struck with wonder, / as were Sarasvatī, Sāvitrī, and the supreme sovereign goddess Pārvatī,

4.124.s:
rohiṇī ca satī saṃjñā svāhādyā devayoṣitaḥ .
muditāḥ prayayuḥ sarvā munipatnyaḥ pativratāḥ .. 33 ..
4.124.d:
रोहिणी च सती संज्ञा स्वाहाद्या देवयोषितः ।
मुदिताः प्रययुः सर्वा मुनिपत्न्यः पतिव्रताः ॥ 33 ॥
4.124.m: Rohiṇī, Satī, Saṃjñā, and the celestial women headed by Svāhā; / all the devoted wives of the munis set forth with delight,

4.124.s:
munayo manavaḥ sarve devāścāpi narāstathā .
śrīkṛṣṇaḥ sa gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ ye cānye prayayurmudā .. 34 ..
4.124.d:
मुनयो मनवः सर्वे देवाश्चापि नरास्तथा ।
श्रीकृष्णः स गणैः सार्धं ये चान्ये प्रययुर्मुदा ॥ 34 ॥
4.124.m: All the munis and Manus, the gods as well as men, / and Śrī Kṛṣṇa along with his attendants and whoever else, set forth joyfully.

4.124.s:
te sarve vividhairdravyaiḥ pūjāṃ cakruḥ śubhakṣaṇe .
baliṣṭhā durbalāścaiva krameṇa ca pṛthakpṛthak .. 35 ..
4.124.d:
ते सर्वे विविधैर्द्रव्यैः पूजां चक्रुः शुभक्षणे ।
बलिष्ठा दुर्बलाश्चैव क्रमेण च पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 35 ॥
4.124.m: They all performed worship with various substances at an auspicious moment, / both the powerful and the weak, gradually and each apart.

4.124.s:
laḍḍukānāṃ ca rāśīnāṃ śatakoṭirbabhūva ha .
śarkarāṇāṃ tadardhaṃ ca svastikānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 36 ..
4.124.d:
लड्डुकानां च राशीनां शतकोटिर्बभूव ह ।
शर्कराणां तदर्धं च स्वस्तिकानां तथैव च ॥ 36 ॥
4.124.m: There were one hundred crores of heaps of sweetmeats, / half of that of sugar, and just as much of svastika pastries.

4.124.s:
annānāṃ bhavyavastūnāṃ śatakoṭirbabhūva ha .
asaṃkhyāni phalānyeva svādūni madhurāṇi ca .. 37 ..
4.124.d:
अन्नानां भव्यवस्तूनां शतकोटिर्बभूव ह ।
असंख्यानि फलान्येव स्वादूनि मधुराणि च ॥ 37 ॥
4.124.m: There were a billion [heaps] of cooked grains and splendid provisions, / and countless delicious and sweet fruits. (37)

4.124.s:
madhukulyā dugdhakulyā dadhikulyā ghṛtasya ca .
babhūvuḥ śatasaṃkhyāśca trailokyānāṃ ca pūjane .. 38 ..
4.124.d:
मधुकुल्या दुग्धकुल्या दधिकुल्या घृतस्य च ।
बभूवुः शतसंख्याश्च त्रैलोक्यानां च पूजने ॥ 38 ॥
4.124.m: Rivulets of honey, rivulets of milk, rivulets of curd, and rivulets of clarified butter / were numbered in the hundreds for the worship by the three worlds. (38)

4.124.s:
pūjāṃ kṛtvā tu te sarve samūṣuśca sukhāsane .
pārvatī paramaprītyā rādhāsthānaṃ samāyayau .. 39 ..
4.124.d:
पूजां कृत्वा तु ते सर्वे समूषुश्च सुखासने ।
पार्वती परमप्रीत्या राधास्थानं समाययौ ॥ 39 ॥
4.124.m: Having performed the worship, they all sat upon comfortable seats. / Pārvatī, with supreme affection, came to the abode of Rādhā. (39)

4.124.s:
sā rādhā pārvatīṃ dṛṣṭvā samutthāya javena ca .
yathāyogyāṃ ca saṃbhāṣāṃ cakāra sādaraṃ mudā .. 40 ..
4.124.d:
सा राधा पार्वतीं दृष्ट्वा समुत्थाय जवेन च ।
यथायोग्यां च संभाषां चकार सादरं मुदा ॥ 40 ॥
4.124.m: Seeing Pārvatī, Rādhā rose quickly / and greeted her fittingly, respectfully and with joy. (40)

4.124.s:
āśleṣaṇaṃ cumbanaṃ ca babhūva ca parasparam .
uvāca madhuraṃ durgā rādhāṃ kṛtvā svavakṣasi .. 41 ..
4.124.d:
आश्लेषणं चुम्बनं च बभूव च परस्परम् ।
उवाच मधुरं दुर्गा राधां कृत्वा स्ववक्षसि ॥ 41 ॥
4.124.m: There was embracing and kissing between them. / Holding Rādhā to her breast, Durgā spoke sweetly: (41)

4.124.s:
pārvatyuvāca
kiṃvā praśnaṃ kariṣyāmi tvāṃ rādhā maṅgalālayām .
gatā te virahajvālā śrīdāmnaḥ śāpamokṣaṇe .. 42 ..
4.124.d:
पार्वत्युवाच
किंवा प्रश्नं करिष्यामि त्वां राधा मङ्गलालयाम् ।
गता ते विरहज्वाला श्रीदाम्नः शापमोक्षणे ॥ 42 ॥
4.124.m: Pārvatī said: / What inquiry shall I make of you, Rādhā, abode of auspiciousness? / The burning torment of your separation has vanished with the release from Śrīdāman's curse. (42)

4.124.s:
satataṃ manmanaḥ prāṇāstvayyeva mayi te tathā .
na hyevamāvayorbhedaḥ śaktipūruṣayostathā .. 43 ..
4.124.d:
सततं मन्मनः प्राणास्त्वय्येव मयि ते तथा ।
न ह्येवमावयोर्भेदः शक्तिपूरुषयोस्तथा ॥ 43 ॥
4.124.m: Constantly my mind and life breaths reside in you alone, and yours in me likewise; / indeed, there is no difference between us, nor between Śakti and Puruṣa. (43)

4.124.s:
yetvāṃ nindanti madbhaktāstvadbhaktāścāpi māmapi .
kumbhīpāke ca pajyante yāvaccandra divākarau .. 44 ..
4.124.d:
येत्वां निन्दन्ति मद्भक्तास्त्वद्भक्ताश्चापि मामपि ।
कुम्भीपाके च पज्यन्ते यावच्चन्द्र दिवाकरौ ॥ 44 ॥
4.124.m: Those devotees of mine who revile you, and your devotees who revile me, / are cooked in the Kumbhīpāka hell as long as the sun and moon endure. (44)

4.124.s:
rādhāmādhavayorbhedaṃ ye kurvanti narādhamāḥ .
vaṃśahānirbhavetteṣāṃ pacyante narake ciram .. 45 ..
4.124.d:
राधामाधवयोर्भेदं ये कुर्वन्ति नराधमाः ।
वंशहानिर्भवेत्तेषां पच्यन्ते नरके चिरम् ॥ 45 ॥
4.124.m: Those vilest of men who make a distinction between Rādhā and Mādhava— / their lineage is destroyed, and they are cooked in hell for a long time. (45)

4.124.s:
yānti sūkarayoniṃ ca pitṛbhiḥ śatakaiḥ saha .
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṭhāyāṃ kṛmayastathā .. 46 ..
4.124.d:
यान्ति सूकरयोनिं च पितृभिः शतकैः सह ।
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि विष्ठायां कृमयस्तथा ॥ 46 ॥
4.124.m: They enter the wombs of swine along with a hundred ancestors, / and live as worms in excrement for sixty thousand years. (46)

4.124.s:
tvayaiva pūjitaḥ putro na mayā ca gaṇeśvaraḥ .
sarvādau sarvapūjyo'yaṃ yathā tava tathā mama .. 47 ..
4.124.d:
त्वयैव पूजितः पुत्रो न मया च गणेश्वरः ।
सर्वादौ सर्वपूज्योऽयं यथा तव तथा मम ॥ 47 ॥
4.124.m: Gaṇeśvara, my son, was worshipped by you, not by me; / he who is to be worshipped first of all by everyone is as much yours as mine. (47)

4.124.s:
yāvajjīvanaparyantaṃ na vicchedo bhaviṣyati .
rādhāmādhavayordevi dugdhadhāvalyayoryathā .. 48 ..
4.124.d:
यावज्जीवनपर्यन्तं न विच्छेदो भविष्यति ।
राधामाधवयोर्देवि दुग्धधावल्ययोर्यथा ॥ 48 ॥
4.124.m: As long as life endures, there will be no separation, / O goddess, between Rādhā and Mādhava, just as between milk and its whiteness. (48)

4.124.s:
siddhāśrame mahātīrthe puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate .
nirvaghnaṃ labhagovindaṃ saṃpūjya vighnakhaṇḍanam .. 49 ..
4.124.d:
सिद्धाश्रमे महातीर्थे पुण्यक्षेत्रे च भारते ।
निर्वघ्नं लभगोविन्दं संपूज्य विघ्नखण्डनम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.124.m: In Siddhāśrama, the great pilgrimage site and holy field in Bhārata, / attain Govinda without obstacle, having fully worshipped the destroyer of obstacles. (49)

4.124.s:
rāseśvarī tvaṃ rasikā śrīkṛṣṇo rasikeśvaraḥ .
vidagdhāyā vidagdhena saṃgamo guṇavānbhadet .. 50 ..
4.124.d:
रासेश्वरी त्वं रसिका श्रीकृष्णो रसिकेश्वरः ।
विदग्धाया विदग्धेन संगमो गुणवान्भदेत् ॥ 50 ॥
4.124.m: You are the queen of the Rāsa dance, relish-filled, and Śrīkṛṣṇa is the lord of relishes; / the union of a clever woman with a clever man is full of virtue. (50)

4.124.s:
śrīdāmnaḥ śāpanirmuktā śatavarṣāntare sati .
kuruṣva madreṇādya kṛṣṇena saha saṃgamam .. 51 ..
4.124.d:
श्रीदाम्नः शापनिर्मुक्ता शतवर्षान्तरे सति ।
कुरुष्व मद्रेणाद्य कृष्णेन सह संगमम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.124.m: Freed from Śrīdāman's curse after a hundred years, O virtuous woman, / unite happily today with Kṛṣṇa. (51)

4.124.s:
mamā''jñayā durlabhayā suveṣaṃ kuru sundari .
sudurlabhaḥ kāminīnāṃ satpuṃsā saha saṃgamaḥ .. 52 ..
4.124.d:
ममा'ऽज्ञया दुर्लभया सुवेषं कुरु सुन्दरि ।
सुदुर्लभः कामिनीनां सत्पुंसा सह संगमः ॥ 52 ॥
4.124.m: By my rare command, adorn yourself well, O beautiful woman; / union with a noble man is exceedingly hard for passionate women to obtain. (52)

4.124.s:
cakruḥ suveṣaṃ rādhāyāḥ priyālyaśca śivājñayā .
ratnasiṃhāsane ramye vāsayāmāsurīśvarīm .. 53 ..
4.124.d:
चक्रुः सुवेषं राधायाः प्रियाल्यश्च शिवाज्ञया ।
रत्नसिंहासने रम्ये वासयामासुरीश्वरीम् ॥ 53 ॥
4.124.m: By Śiva's command, the dear companions adorned Rādhā splendidly / and seated the sovereign goddess upon a charming, jewelled throne. (53)

4.124.s:
purato ratnamālā sā ratnamālāṃ gale dadau .
rādhāyā dakṣiṇe haste krīḍāpadmaṃ manoharam .. 54 ..
4.124.d:
पुरतो रत्नमाला सा रत्नमालां गले ददौ ।
राधाया दक्षिणे हस्ते क्रीडापद्मं मनोहरम् ॥ 54 ॥
4.124.m: In front [of her], Ratnamālā placed a garland of jewels upon her neck, / and a charming play-lotus in Rādhā's right hand. (54)

4.124.s:
dadau padmamukhī pādapadmayugme'pyalaktakam .
pradadau sundarī gopī sindūraṃ sundaraṃ varam .. 55 ..
4.124.d:
ददौ पद्ममुखी पादपद्मयुग्मेऽप्यलक्तकम् ।
प्रददौ सुन्दरी गोपी सिन्दूरं सुन्दरं वरम् ॥ 55 ॥
4.124.m: Padmamukhī applied red lac to her pair of lotus feet, / and a beautiful gopī applied splendid, excellent red vermilion, (55)

4.124.s:
candanena samayutaṃ sīmantādhaḥ sthalojjvalam .
sucārukabarīṃ ramyāṃ cakāra mālatī satī .. 56 ..
4.124.d:
चन्दनेन समयुतं सीमन्ताधः स्थलोज्ज्वलम् ।
सुचारुकबरीं रम्यां चकार मालती सती ॥ 56 ॥
4.124.m: mixed with sandalwood, radiant beneath the parting of her hair; / the virtuous Mālatī arranged her lovely hair into a very charming braid, (56)

4.124.s:
manoharāṃ munīnāṃ ca mālatīmālyabhūṣitām .
kastūrīkuṅkumāktaṃ ca cārucandanapatrakam .. 57 ..
4.124.d:
मनोहरां मुनीनां च मालतीमाल्यभूषिताम् ।
कस्तूरीकुङ्कुमाक्तं च चारुचन्दनपत्रकम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.124.m: captivating even to sages, adorned with garlands of jasmine; / and the virtuous Candanā drew decorative leaf designs of lovely sandalwood paste, (57)

4.124.s:
stanayugme sukaṭhine cakāra candanā satī .
cārucampakapuppāṇāṃ mālāṃ gandhamanoharām .. 58 ..
4.124.d:
स्तनयुग्मे सुकठिने चकार चन्दना सती ।
चारुचम्पकपुप्पाणां मालां गन्धमनोहराम् ॥ 58 ॥
4.124.m: smeared with musk and saffron, upon her exceedingly firm pair of breasts. / Mālāvatī gave her a garland of lovely campaka flowers, (58)

4.124.s:
mālāvatī dadau tasyau praphullāṃ navamallikām .
ratīṣu rasikā gopī ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitām .. 59 ..
4.124.d:
मालावती ददौ तस्यौ प्रफुल्लां नवमल्लिकाम् ।
रतीषु रसिका गोपी रत्नभूषणभूषिताम् ॥ 59 ॥
4.124.m: delightful with fragrance, and blooming fresh mallikā blossoms. / A gopī skilled in love-sports adorned her with jewelled ornaments; (59)

4.124.s:
tāṃ cakārātirasikāṃ varāṃ ratirasotsukām .
śaratpadmadalābhaṃ ca lojanaṃ kajjalojjvalam .. 60 ..
4.124.d:
तां चकारातिरसिकां वरां रतिरसोत्सुकाम् ।
शरत्पद्मदलाभं च लोजनं कज्जलोज्ज्वलम् ॥ 60 ॥
4.124.m: she made her, who was eager for the delight of love, deeply impassioned and exquisite. / Having made her eyes, radiant like autumn lotus petals, bright with collyrium, (60)

4.124.s:
kṛtvā dadau sulalitaṃ vastraṃ ca lalitā satī .
mahendreṇa pradattaṃ ca pārijātaprasūnakam .. 61 ..
4.124.d:
कृत्वा ददौ सुललितं वस्त्रं च ललिता सती ।
महेन्द्रेण प्रदत्तं च पारिजातप्रसूनकम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.124.m: the virtuous Lalitā gave her very elegant garments. / She placed in her hand fragrant pārijāta blossoms, (61)

4.124.s:
sugandhiyuktaṃ tasyāśca pārijātaṃ kare dadau .
suśīlaṃ madhuroktaṃ ca bhartuḥ pārśve yathocitam .. 62 ..
4.124.d:
सुगन्धियुक्तं तस्याश्च पारिजातं करे ददौ ।
सुशीलं मधुरोक्तं च भर्तुः पार्श्वे यथोचितम् ॥ 62 ॥
4.124.m: given by Mahendra, together with perfume. / Good conduct, sweet speech, and what is appropriate before a husband— (62)

4.124.s:
śikṣāṃ cakāra nītiṃ ca suśīlā gopikā satī .
strīṇāṃ ca ṣoḍaśakalāṃ vipattau vismṛtāṃtayoḥ .. 63 ..
4.124.d:
शिक्षां चकार नीतिं च सुशीला गोपिका सती ।
स्त्रीणां च षोडशकलां विपत्तौ विस्मृतांतयोः ॥ 63 ॥
4.124.m: such instruction and proper behaviour the virtuous cowherd woman Suśīlā provided. / The sixteen arts of women, forgotten by the two in their misfortune, (63)

4.124.s:
smaraṇaṃ kārayāmāsa rādhāmātā kalāvatī .
śrṛṅgāraviṣayoktaṃ ca vacanaṃ ca sudhopamam .. 64 ..
4.124.d:
स्मरणं कारयामास राधामाता कलावती ।
श्रृङ्गारविषयोक्तं च वचनं च सुधोपमम् ॥ 64 ॥
4.124.m: Kalāvatī, Rādhā's mother, caused her to recall; / and words nectar-like regarding the nature of erotic love, (64)

4.124.s:
smaraṇaṃ kārayāmāsa bhaginī ca sudhāmukhī .
kamalānāṃ campakānāṃ dale candanacarcite .. 65 ..
4.124.d:
स्मरणं कारयामास भगिनी च सुधामुखी ।
कमलानां चम्पकानां दले चन्दनचर्चिते ॥ 65 ॥
4.124.m: her sister Sudhāmukhī caused her to remember. / Upon petals of lotuses and campakas smeared with sandalwood paste, (65)

4.124.s:
cakāra ratitalpaṃ ca kamalā cā''śu komalam .
cārucampakapuṣpaṃ ca kṛṣṇārthaṃ puṭakasthitam .. 66 ..
4.124.d:
चकार रतितल्पं च कमला चा'ऽशु कोमलम् ।
चारुचम्पकपुष्पं च कृष्णार्थं पुटकस्थितम् ॥ 66 ॥
4.124.m: Kamalā swiftly prepared a soft bed for amorous delight. / And the virtuous Pārvatī herself placed lovely campaka flowers in a cup for Kṛṣṇa, (66)

4.124.s:
cakāra candanāktaṃ ca svayaṃ ca pārvatī satī .
puṣpaṃ kelikadambānāṃ stabakaṃ ca manoharam .. 67 ..
4.124.d:
चकार चन्दनाक्तं च स्वयं च पार्वती सती ।
पुष्पं केलिकदम्बानां स्तबकं च मनोहरम् ॥ 67 ॥
4.124.m: smeared with sandalwood, and a charming cluster / of blossoms from play-kadamba trees; (67)

4.124.s:
kadambamālāṃ kṛṣṇārtha vidyamānāṃ cakāra sā .
tāmbūlaṃ ca varaṃ samyaṃ karpūrādisuvāsitam .. 68 ..
4.124.d:
कदम्बमालां कृष्णार्थ विद्यमानां चकार सा ।
ताम्बूलं च वरं सम्यं कर्पूरादिसुवासितम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.124.m: she prepared a garland of kadamba blossoms for Kṛṣṇa. / And excellent betel, properly perfumed with camphor and the like, (68)

4.124.s:
kṛṣṇapriyā ca kṛṣṇārthaṃ cakāra vāsitaṃ jalam .
etasminnantare sarvamāśramaṃ sajalasthalam .. 69 ..
4.124.d:
कृष्णप्रिया च कृष्णार्थं चकार वासितं जलम् ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे सर्वमाश्रमं सजलस्थलम् ॥ 69 ॥
4.124.m: and fragrant water, Kṛṣṇa's beloved prepared for Kṛṣṇa's sake. / Meanwhile, the entire hermitage, both water and land, (69)

4.124.s:
sākṣādgorocanābhaṃ ca dadṛśurmunayaḥ surāḥ .
te sarve vismayaṃ gatvā papracchuḥ kṛṣṇamīśvaram .. 70 ..
4.124.d:
साक्षाद्गोरोचनाभं च ददृशुर्मुनयः सुराः ।
ते सर्वे विस्मयं गत्वा पप्रच्छुः कृष्णमीश्वरम् ॥ 70 ॥
4.124.m: the sages and gods beheld shining like actual gorocanā. / Filled with wonder, they all questioned the lord Kṛṣṇa. (70)

4.124.s: uvāca bhagavāṃstāśca sarvajñaḥ sarvakārāṇā .. 71 ..
4.124.d: उवाच भगवांस्ताश्च सर्वज्ञः सर्वकाराणा ॥ 71 ॥
4.124.m: The Blessed Lord, omniscient, the cause of all, spoke to them: (71)

4.124.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
abhiśaptā ca śrīdāmnā bhraṣṭaśobhā rādhikā .
sarvaṃ jñānaṃ visasmāra madvicchedajvarāturā .. 72 ..
4.124.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
अभिशप्ता च श्रीदाम्ना भ्रष्टशोभा राधिका ।
सर्वं ज्ञानं विसस्मार मद्विच्छेदज्वरातुरा ॥ 72 ॥
4.124.m: The Blessed Lord said: / Cursed by Śrīdāman, Rādhikā lost her splendour; / afflicted with the fever of separation from me, she forgot all knowledge. (72)

4.124.s:
vimukte varṣaśatake jñānaṃ sasmāra sā satī .
siddhāśramaṃ ca pītābhaṃ rāseśvaryāśca tejasā .. 73 ..
4.124.d:
विमुक्ते वर्षशतके ज्ञानं सस्मार सा सती ।
सिद्धाश्रमं च पीताभं रासेश्वर्याश्च तेजसा ॥ 73 ॥
4.124.m: Now that the hundred years have passed, that virtuous woman has remembered her knowledge, / and Siddhāśrama has become golden-yellow with the radiance of the queen of the Rāsa dance— (73)

4.124.s:
paramāhlādakaṃ tejaścandrakoṭisamaprabham .
sukhadṛśyaṃ ca sukhadaṃ cakṣudhāṃ prāṇināmapi .. 74 ..
4.124.d:
परमाह्लादकं तेजश्चन्द्रकोटिसमप्रभम् ।
सुखदृश्यं च सुखदं चक्षुधां प्राणिनामपि ॥ 74 ॥
4.124.m: a supremely joyful radiance, equal in splendor to ten million moons, / pleasant to behold and bestowing delight upon the eyes of all living beings. (74)

4.124.s:
tacchrutvā paramāścaryaṃ munayo manavastathā .
devyaśca sarvadevāste brahmeśānādayastathā .. 75 ..
4.124.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा परमाश्चर्यं मुनयो मनवस्तथा ।
देव्यश्च सर्वदेवास्ते ब्रह्मेशानादयस्तथा ॥ 75 ॥
4.124.m: Hearing that, the sages, the Manus, / the goddesses, and all the gods, headed by Brahmā and Īśāna, (75)

4.124.s:
javena gatvā tatsthānaṃ bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharā .
sarve janāste dadṛśustrailokyasthāśca rādhikām .. 76 ..
4.124.d:
जवेन गत्वा तत्स्थानं भक्तिनम्रात्मकंधरा ।
सर्वे जनास्ते ददृशुस्त्रैलोक्यस्थाश्च राधिकाम् ॥ 76 ॥
4.124.m: went swiftly to that place, their necks bowed with devotion. / All those people dwelling in the three worlds beheld Rādhikā, (76)

4.124.s:
śvetacampakavarṇābhāmatulāṃ sumanoharām .
mohinīṃ mānasānāṃ ca munīnāmūrdhvaretasām .. 77 ..
4.124.d:
श्वेतचम्पकवर्णाभामतुलां सुमनोहराम् ।
मोहिनीं मानसानां च मुनीनामूर्ध्वरेतसाम् ॥ 77 ॥
4.124.m: who had the complexion of a white campaka flower, peerless and very enchanting, / enchanting the minds of even celibate sages, (77)

4.124.s:
sukeśīṃ sundarīṃ śyāmāṃ nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalām .
nitambakaṭhinaśroṇīṃ stanayugmonnatānanām .. 78 ..
4.124.d:
सुकेशीं सुन्दरीं श्यामां न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डलाम् ।
नितम्बकठिनश्रोणीं स्तनयुग्मोन्नताननाम् ॥ 78 ॥
4.124.m: having beautiful hair, shapely, youthful, with proportions of a banyan tree, / with rounded, firm hips, and a face uplifted towards her pair of breasts; (78)

4.124.s:
koṭīnduninditāsyāṃ tāṃ sasmitāṃ sudatīṃ satīm .
kajjalojjvalarūpāṃ ca śaratkamalalojanām .. 79 ..
4.124.d:
कोटीन्दुनिन्दितास्यां तां सस्मितां सुदतीं सतीम् ।
कज्जलोज्ज्वलरूपां च शरत्कमललोजनाम् ॥ 79 ॥
4.124.m: whose face surpassed ten million moons, smiling, with beautiful teeth, virtuous, / radiant with collyrium, with eyes like autumn lotuses; (79)

4.124.s:
mahālakṣmīṃ bījarūpāṃ parāmādyāṃ sanātīm .
paramātmasvarūpasya prāṇādhiṣṭhātṛdevatām .. 80 ..
4.124.d:
महालक्ष्मीं बीजरूपां परामाद्यां सनातीम् ।
परमात्मस्वरूपस्य प्राणाधिष्ठातृदेवताम् ॥ 80 ॥
4.124.m: Mahālakṣmī, the seed-form, the supreme, primordial, eternal goddess, / the presiding deity over the life breaths of the Paramātman himself; (80)

4.124.s:
stutāṃ ca pūjitāṃ caiva parāṃ ca paramātmane .
brahmasvarūpāṃ nirliptāṃ nityarūpāṃ ca nirguṇām .. 81 ..
4.124.d:
स्तुतां च पूजितां चैव परां च परमात्मने ।
ब्रह्मस्वरूपां निर्लिप्तां नित्यरूपां च निर्गुणाम् ॥ 81 ॥
4.124.m: praised and worshipped, supreme to the Paramātman, / whose nature is Brahman, unattached, eternal in form, and devoid of gunas; (81)

4.124.s:
viśvānurodhātprakṛtiṃ bhaktānugrahavigrahām .
matyasvarūpāṃ śuddhāṃ ca pūtāṃ patitapāvanīm .. 82 ..
4.124.d:
विश्वानुरोधात्प्रकृतिं भक्तानुग्रहविग्रहाम् ।
मत्यस्वरूपां शुद्धां च पूतां पतितपावनीम् ॥ 82 ॥
4.124.m: Prakṛti for the sake of the universe, embodied out of grace to devotees, / whose nature is truth, pure, consecrated, and purifier of the fallen. (82)

4.124.s:
sutīrthapūtāṃ satkīrtiṃ vidhātrīṃ vedasāmapi .
mahatpriyāṃ ca mahatīṃ mahāviṣṇośca mātaram .. 83 ..
4.124.d:
सुतीर्थपूतां सत्कीर्तिं विधात्रीं वेदसामपि ।
महत्प्रियां च महतीं महाविष्णोश्च मातरम् ॥ 83 ॥
4.124.m: I praise her who is purified by sacred bathing-places, of noble renown, the creator even of the creators, / dear to the Great One, herself great, and the mother of Mahāviṣṇu;

4.124.s:
rāseśvareśvarīṃ ramyāṃ rasikāṃ rasikeśvarīm .
vahniśuddhāṃśukādhāmāṃ svecchārūpāṃ śubhālayām .. 84 ..
4.124.d:
रासेश्वरेश्वरीं रम्यां रसिकां रसिकेश्वरीम् ।
वह्निशुद्धांशुकाधामां स्वेच्छारूपां शुभालयाम् ॥ 84 ॥
4.124.m: the sovereign lady of the lord of the rāsa dance, charming, appreciative of aesthetic delight, queen of the connoisseurs of love, / whose abode consists of garments pure as fire, who assumes forms at her own will, an auspicious dwelling;

4.124.s:
gopībhiḥ saptabhiḥ śaśvatsevitāṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ .
catasṛbhiḥ priyālībhiḥ pādapadmopasevitām .. 85 ..
4.124.d:
गोपीभिः सप्तभिः शश्वत्सेवितां श्वेतचामरैः ।
चतसृभिः प्रियालीभिः पादपद्मोपसेविताम् ॥ 85 ॥
4.124.m: who is constantly served by seven cowherd maidens with white cāmaras, / whose lotus-feet are attended to by four beloved companions;

4.124.s:
amūlyaratnanirmāṇabhūṣaṇoccairvibhūṣitām .
cārukuṇḍalayugmena śrutigaṇḍasthalojjvalām .. 86 ..
4.124.d:
अमूल्यरत्ननिर्माणभूषणोच्चैर्विभूषिताम् ।
चारुकुण्डलयुग्मेन श्रुतिगण्डस्थलोज्ज्वलाम् ॥ 86 ॥
4.124.m: splendidly adorned with ornaments fashioned from priceless gems, / bright at the temples and ears with a lovely pair of ear-ornaments;

4.124.s:
sunāsāṃ gajamuktārhāṃ khagendracañcuninditām .
kuṅkumālaktakastūrīsnigdhacandanacarcitām .. 87 ..
4.124.d:
सुनासां गजमुक्तार्हां खगेन्द्रचञ्चुनिन्दिताम् ।
कुङ्कुमालक्तकस्तूरीस्निग्धचन्दनचर्चिताम् ॥ 87 ॥
4.124.m: with a shapely nose worthy of an elephant-pearl, mocking the beak of the king of birds, / anointed with fragrant saffron, lac-dye, musk, and cool sandalwood;

4.124.s:
dadhānāṃ sukapolaṃ ca komalāṅgīṃ sukāmukīm .
gacendragāminīṃ rāmāṃ kāmanīyāṃ sukāminīm .. 88 ..
4.124.d:
दधानां सुकपोलं च कोमलाङ्गीं सुकामुकीम् ।
गचेन्द्रगामिनीं रामां कामनीयां सुकामिनीम् ॥ 88 ॥
4.124.m: bearing lovely cheeks, soft-limbed, very passionate, / walking like the king of elephants, delighting, desirable, and passionately loving;

4.124.s:
kāmāstrajayarūpāṃ ca kāmakāmyālayāṃ varām .
krīḍākamalamamlānaṃ pārijātaprasūnakam .. 89 ..
4.124.d:
कामास्त्रजयरूपां च कामकाम्यालयां वराम् ।
क्रीडाकमलमम्लानं पारिजातप्रसूनकम् ॥ 89 ॥
4.124.m: whose form vanquishes the weapons of Kāma, an excellent dwelling of desires and things wished for; / [holding] an unfading play-lotus, a blossom of the pārijāta tree,

4.124.s:
amūlyaratnanirmāṇaṃ dadhānāṃ darpaṇojjvalam .
nānāratnavicitrāḍhyaratanasiṃhāsanasthitām .. 90 ..
4.124.d:
अमूल्यरत्ननिर्माणं दधानां दर्पणोज्ज्वलम् ।
नानारत्नविचित्राढ्यरतनसिंहासनस्थिताम् ॥ 90 ॥
4.124.m: and holding a bright mirror fashioned of priceless jewels; / seated upon a jewel-throne enriched with various wondrous gems;

4.124.s:
padmaiḥ padmārcitaṃ pādapadmaṃ ca maṅgalālayam .
hṛtpadme dhyāyamānaṃ ca kṛṇasya paramātmanaḥ .. 91 ..
4.124.d:
पद्मैः पद्मार्चितं पादपद्मं च मङ्गलालयम् ।
हृत्पद्मे ध्यायमानं च कृणस्य परमात्मनः ॥ 91 ॥
4.124.m: whose lotus-foot, an abode of auspiciousness, is worshipped with lotuses by Lakṣmī, / and who meditates within her lotus-heart upon the Paramātman Kṛṣṇa;

4.124.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā svapne jāgaraṇe'pi ca .
tatprītiṃ prema saubhāgyaṃ smarantīṃ nityanūtanam .. 92 ..
4.124.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा स्वप्ने जागरणेऽपि च ।
तत्प्रीतिं प्रेम सौभाग्यं स्मरन्तीं नित्यनूतनम् ॥ 92 ॥
4.124.m: remembering in action, mind, and speech, in dream as well as waking, / his affection, love, and good fortune, which is ever new;

4.124.s:
bhāvānuraktasaṃsaktāṃ śuddhabhaktāṃ pativratām .
dhanyāṃ mānyāṃ gauravarṇāṃ śaśvadvakṣaḥ sthalasthitām .. 93 ..
4.124.d:
भावानुरक्तसंसक्तां शुद्धभक्तां पतिव्रताम् ।
धन्यां मान्यां गौरवर्णां शश्वद्वक्षः स्थलस्थिताम् ॥ 93 ॥
4.124.m: attached and devoted in love, a pure devotee, a devoted wife, / blessed, revered, golden-complexioned, dwelling constantly upon his chest;

4.124.s:
priyāsu priyabhakteṣu supriyāṃ priyavādinīm .
kṛṣṇavāmāṅgasaṃbhūtāmabhedāṃ guṇarūpayoḥ .. 94 ..
4.124.d:
प्रियासु प्रियभक्तेषु सुप्रियां प्रियवादिनीम् ।
कृष्णवामाङ्गसंभूतामभेदां गुणरूपयोः ॥ 94 ॥
4.124.m: the dearest among beloved women, among dear devotees, speaking sweetly, / born from the left half of Kṛṣṇa's body, non-different in qualities and form;

4.124.s:
golokavāsinīṃ devadevīṃ sarvoparisthitam .
vṛṣabhānasutākhyāṃ tāṃ puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate .. 95 ..
4.124.d:
गोलोकवासिनीं देवदेवीं सर्वोपरिस्थितम् ।
वृषभानसुताख्यां तां पुण्यक्षेत्रे च भारते ॥ 95 ॥
4.124.m: dwelling in Goloka, goddess of gods, standing supreme above all, / known as the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu in the sacred land of Bhārata;

4.124.s:
gopīśvarīṃ guptarūpāṃ siddhidāṃ siddhirūpiṇīm .
dhyānāsādhyāṃ durārādhyāṃ vande sadbhaktavanditām .. 96 ..
4.124.d:
गोपीश्वरीं गुप्तरूपां सिद्धिदां सिद्धिरूपिणीम् ।
ध्यानासाध्यां दुराराध्यां वन्दे सद्भक्तवन्दिताम् ॥ 96 ॥
4.124.m: the mistress of the cowherdesses, of secret form, the bestower of perfection, the embodiment of perfection, / unapproachable through meditation, difficult to propitiate: I praise her who is extolled by true devotees.

4.124.s:
dhyāne dhyānena rādhāyā vyāyante dhyānatatparāḥ .
ihaiva jīvanmuktāste paratra kṛṣṇapārṣadāḥ .. 97 ..
4.124.d:
ध्याने ध्यानेन राधाया व्यायन्ते ध्यानतत्पराः ।
इहैव जीवन्मुक्तास्ते परत्र कृष्णपार्षदाः ॥ 97 ॥
4.124.m: Those intent on meditation, who meditate through meditation upon Rādhā, / are liberated while living even in this world, and become companions of Kṛṣṇa in the next.

4.124.s:
dṛṣṭvā brahmā ca sarvādau tuṣṭāva parameśvarīm .
svayaṃ vidhātā jagatāṃ mātaraṃ vedhasāmapi .. 98 ..
4.124.d:
दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मा च सर्वादौ तुष्टाव परमेश्वरीम् ।
स्वयं विधाता जगतां मातरं वेधसामपि ॥ 98 ॥
4.124.m: Seeing her, Brahmā first of all praised the supreme goddess— / himself the creator of the worlds, [praising] the mother even of the creators.

4.124.s:
brāhmovāca
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasraṇi divyāni parameśvari .
puṣkare ca tapastaptaṃ puṇyakṣetre ca bhārate .. 99 ..
4.124.d:
ब्राह्मोवाच
षष्टिवर्षसहस्रणि दिव्यानि परमेश्वरि ।
पुष्करे च तपस्तप्तं पुण्यक्षेत्रे च भारते ॥ 99 ॥
4.124.m:
Brahmā said:
For sixty thousand divine years, O supreme goddess, / austerity was performed by me at Puṣkara in the sacred land of Bhārata.

4.124.s:
tvatpādapadmadhuramadhulubdhena cetasā .
madhuvratena lolena preritena mayā sati .. 100 ..
4.124.d:
त्वत्पादपद्मधुरमधुलुब्धेन चेतसा ।
मधुव्रतेन लोलेन प्रेरितेन मया सति ॥ 100 ॥
4.124.m: With a mind greedy for the sweet nectar of your lotus-feet, / driven like a restless bee, O virtuous lady,

4.124.s:
tathā'pi na mayā labdhaṃ tvatpādapadmamīpsitam .
na dṛṣṭamapi svapne'yi jātā vāgaśarīriṇī .. 101 ..
4.124.d:
तथाऽपि न मया लब्धं त्वत्पादपद्ममीप्सितम् ।
न दृष्टमपि स्वप्नेऽयि जाता वागशरीरिणी ॥ 101 ॥
4.124.m: still your desired lotus-foot was not obtained by me, / nor even seen in a dream; then an incorporeal voice arose:

4.124.s:
vārāhe bhārate varṣe puṇye vṛndāvane vane .
siddhāśrame gaṇeśasya pādapadmaṃ ca drakṣyasi .. 102 ..
4.124.d:
वाराहे भारते वर्षे पुण्ये वृन्दावने वने ।
सिद्धाश्रमे गणेशस्य पादपद्मं च द्रक्ष्यसि ॥ 102 ॥
4.124.m: “In the Vārāha kalpa, in the land of Bhārata, in the holy forest of Vṛndāvana, / at Siddhāśrama, you will behold the lotus-foot of Gaṇeśa.

4.124.s:
rādhāmādhavayordāsyaṃ kuto viṣayiṇastava .
nivartasva mahābhāga parametatmudurlabham .. 103 ..
4.124.d:
राधामाधवयोर्दास्यं कुतो विषयिणस्तव ।
निवर्तस्व महाभाग परमेतत्मुदुर्लभम् ॥ 103 ॥
4.124.m: How could servitude to Rādhā and Mādhava belong to you, an involved worldly being? / Turn back, O blessed one; this supreme state is exceedingly rare.”

4.124.s:
iti śrutvā nivṛtto'haṃ tapase bhagnamānasaḥ .
paripurṇa tadadhunā vāñchitaṃ tapasaḥ phalam .. 104 ..
4.124.d:
इति श्रुत्वा निवृत्तोऽहं तपसे भग्नमानसः ।
परिपुर्ण तदधुना वाञ्छितं तपसः फलम् ॥ 104 ॥
4.124.m: Hearing this, I turned back with a broken heart from austerity; / now that desired fruit of my austerity is completely fulfilled.

4.124.s:
mahādeva uvāca
padmaiḥ padmārcitaṃ pādapadamaṃ yasya sudurlabham .
dhyāyante dhyānaniṣṭhāśca śāśvadrabrahmādayaḥ surāḥ .. 105 ..
4.124.d:
महादेव उवाच
पद्मैः पद्मार्चितं पादपदमं यस्य सुदुर्लभम् ।
ध्यायन्ते ध्याननिष्ठाश्च शाश्वद्रब्रह्मादयः सुराः ॥ 105 ॥
4.124.m:
Mahādeva said:
Whose lotus-foot, exceedingly difficult to attain, is worshipped by Lakṣmī with lotuses, / and is constantly contemplated by Brahmā and the other gods steadfast in meditation,

4.124.s:
munayo manavaścaiva siddhāḥ santaśca yoginaḥ .
draṣṭuṃ naiva kṣamāḥ svapne bhavatī tasya vakṣasi .. 106 ..
4.124.d:
मुनयो मनवश्चैव सिद्धाः सन्तश्च योगिनः ।
द्रष्टुं नैव क्षमाः स्वप्ने भवती तस्य वक्षसि ॥ 106 ॥
4.124.m: and whom the sages, the Manus, the perfected ones, the saints, and the yogins / are not able to behold even in a dream—you yourself [dwell] on his chest.

4.124.s:
ananta uvāca
vedāśca vedamātā ca purāṇāni ca suvrate .
ahaṃ sarasvatī santa stotuṃ nālaṃ ca saṃtatam .. 107 ..
4.124.d:
अनन्त उवाच
वेदाश्च वेदमाता च पुराणानि च सुव्रते ।
अहं सरस्वती सन्त स्तोतुं नालं च संततम् ॥ 107 ॥
4.124.m:
Ananta said:
O lady of virtuous vows, the Vedas, the Mother of the Vedas, the Purāṇas, / myself, Sarasvatī, and the saints are never capable of adequately praising you.

4.124.s:
asmākaṃ stavane yasya bhrūbhaṅgaṃ ca sudurlabham .
tavaiva bhatsene bhītāścāvayorantaraṃ hareḥ .. 108 ..
4.124.d:
अस्माकं स्तवने यस्य भ्रूभङ्गं च सुदुर्लभम् ।
तवैव भत्सेने भीताश्चावयोरन्तरं हरेः ॥ 108 ॥
4.124.m: Even a knitted eyebrow of his is exceedingly difficult for us to attain through our praise, / yet he is terrified by your scolding; such is the difference between us two and Hari.

4.124.s:
evaṃ devāśca devyaścāpyanye ye ca samāgatāḥ .
praṇatāstuṣṭuvuḥ sarve munimanvādayastathā .. 109 ..
4.124.d:
एवं देवाश्च देव्यश्चाप्यन्ये ये च समागताः ।
प्रणतास्तुष्टुवुः सर्वे मुनिमन्वादयस्तथा ॥ 109 ॥
4.124.m: Thus the gods, goddesses, and others who had arrived, / bowing down, along with the sages, Manus, and others, all uttered praises.

4.124.s:
lajjayā namravaktrāśca rukmiṇyadyāśca yoṣitaḥ .
malīmasaṃ ca cakrustāḥ śvāsena ratnadarpaṇam .. 110 ..
4.124.d:
लज्जया नम्रवक्त्राश्च रुक्मिण्यद्याश्च योषितः ।
मलीमसं च चक्रुस्ताः श्वासेन रत्नदर्पणम् ॥ 110 ॥
4.124.m: With faces lowered in shame, Rukmiṇī and the other women / clouded their jewel-mirrors with their sighs.

4.124.s:
mṛtatulyā satyabhāmā nirāhārā kṛśodarī .
manaso'pyabhimānaṃ ca sarva tatyāca nārada .. 111 ..
4.124.d:
मृततुल्या सत्यभामा निराहारा कृशोदरी ।
मनसोऽप्यभिमानं च सर्व तत्याच नारद ॥ 111 ॥
4.124.m: Satyabhāmā, like one dead, taking no food, her belly emaciated, / cast away all pride from her mind, O Nārada.

4.124.s:
iti śrībrahmao mahāo śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhao uttao nāradanāo
siddhāśramatīrthayātrāprasaṅgegaṇeśapūjanaṃ brahmeśaśeṣādikṛtarādhikāstotraṃ nāma
caturviṃśatyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 124 ..
4.124.d:
इति श्रीब्रह्मओ महाओ श्रीकृष्णजन्मखओ उत्तओ नारदनाओ
सिद्धाश्रमतीर्थयात्राप्रसङ्गेगणेशपूजनं ब्रह्मेशशेषादिकृतराधिकास्तोत्रं नाम
चतुर्विंशत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 124 ॥
4.124.m: Thus ends the one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter, entitled “The Worship of Gaṇeśa in the Context of the Pilgrimage to Siddhāśrama and the Hymn of Praise to Rādhikā by Brahmā, Īśa, Śeṣa, and Others,” in the latter part of the Śrīkṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa of the great Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, in the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa.

4.125.s:
nārada uvāca
gaṇeśapūjanādeva rādhāstotrātparaṃ vibho .
babhūva kiṃ rahasyaṃ vā tanme vyākhyātumarhasi .. 1 ..
4.125.d:
नारद उवाच
गणेशपूजनादेव राधास्तोत्रात्परं विभो ।
बभूव किं रहस्यं वा तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥ 1 ॥

4.125.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca
gaśeśapūjane tīrthe ye devāśca samāyayuḥ .
munayaścāpi yogīndrā vasanto vaṭamūlake .. 2 ..
4.125.d:
नारायण उवाच
गशेशपूजने तीर्थे ये देवाश्च समाययुः ।
मुनयश्चापि योगीन्द्रा वसन्तो वटमूलके ॥ 2 ॥
4.125.m:
Nārāyaṇa said:
The gods who came to the sacred place for the worship of Gaṇeśa, / and the sages and lords of yogins dwelling at the foot of the banyan tree,

4.125.s:
vasudevo devakī ca paramādarabūrvakam .
papraccha śaṃbhuṃ brāhmaṇamanantaṃ munipuṃgavān .. 3 ..
4.125.d:
वसुदेवो देवकी च परमादरबूर्वकम् ।
पप्रच्छ शंभुं ब्राह्मणमनन्तं मुनिपुंगवान् ॥ 3 ॥
4.125.m: to them Vasudeva and Devakī, with the utmost respect, / asked Śambhu, Brahmā, Ananta, and the foremost sages:

4.125.s:
bhavedbhavābdhitaraṇamāvayoruttamā gatiḥ .
śīghraṃ brūta mahābhāgā dīnayordīnabāndhavāḥ .. 4 ..
4.125.d:
भवेद्भवाब्धितरणमावयोरुत्तमा गतिः ।
शीघ्रं ब्रूत महाभागा दीनयोर्दीनबान्धवाः ॥ 4 ॥
4.125.m: “How may crossing the ocean of worldly existence and the highest destination be ours? / Tell us quickly, O blessed ones, you who are friends to the wretched!

4.125.s:
bhavābdhitaraṇe taryāṃ tatra yūyaṃ ca nāvikāḥ .
na hyammayāni tīrthāni na devā mṛcchilāmayāḥ .. 5 ..
4.125.d:
भवाब्धितरणे तर्यां तत्र यूयं च नाविकाः ।
न ह्यम्मयानि तीर्थानि न देवा मृच्छिलामयाः ॥ 5 ॥
4.125.m: You are the boatmen for our boat in crossing the ocean of worldly existence. / Indeed, sacred places are not merely made of water, nor are gods made of clay and stone;

4.125.s:
yajñarūpāṇi puṇyāni vratānyanaśanāni ca .
tapāṃsi nānādānāni vipradevārcanāni ca .. 6 ..
4.125.d:
यज्ञरूपाणि पुण्यानि व्रतान्यनशनानि च ।
तपांसि नानादानानि विप्रदेवार्चनानि च ॥ 6 ॥
4.125.m: merits in the form of sacrifices, vows, fasting, / austerities, various gifts, and the worship of brāhmaṇas and gods—

4.125.s:
ciraṃ punanti sarvāṇi darśanādeva vaiṣṇavāḥ .
satāṃ ca viṣṇubhaktānāṃ rajasāṃ sparśamātrataḥ .. 7 ..
4.125.d:
चिरं पुनन्ति सर्वाणि दर्शनादेव वैष्णवाः ।
सतां च विष्णुभक्तानां रजसां स्पर्शमात्रतः ॥ 7 ॥
4.125.m: all these purify over a long time, whereas Vaiṣṇavas purify simply by being seen. / By the mere touch of the dust of the virtuous devotees of Viṣṇu,

4.125.s:
pūtānāṃ pādapadmānāṃ sadyaḥ pūtā vasuṃdharā .
tīrthāni ca pavitrāṇi samudrāḥ parvatāstathā .. 8 ..
4.125.d:
पूतानां पादपद्मानां सद्यः पूता वसुंधरा ।
तीर्थानि च पवित्राणि समुद्राः पर्वतास्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
4.125.m: of their purified lotus-feet, the earth is instantly purified, / as well as sacred waters, oceans, and mountains.

4.125.s:
surā darśanamicchanti pātakendhanapāpakam .
so'jñāni naiva bubudhe jñānaṃ ca jñāninā saha .. 9 ..
4.125.d:
सुरा दर्शनमिच्छन्ति पातकेन्धनपापकम् ।
सोऽज्ञानि नैव बुबुधे ज्ञानं च ज्ञानिना सह ॥ 9 ॥
4.125.m: The gods desire their sight, which is a fire to the fuel of sins. / Yet this ignorant man, dwelling with the wise, did not understand knowledge,

4.125.s:
paramaṃ svādurūpaṃ ca dadhidugdharasaṃ yathā .
yathā kṛṇasya tāto'haṃ saṅgī sucirameva ca .. 10 ..
4.125.d:
परमं स्वादुरूपं च दधिदुग्धरसं यथा ।
यथा कृणस्य तातोऽहं सङ्गी सुचिरमेव च ॥ 10 ॥
4.125.m: just as one does not realize how supremely sweet the taste of curd and milk is! / Though I am Kṛṣṇa's father and have been his companion for a very long time,

4.125.s:
tathaiva devakī mātā jñānināṃ ca gurorguroḥ .
vasudevavacaḥ śrutvā prahasya śaṃkaraḥ svayam
caturṇāmapi vedānāmuvāca janako guruḥ .. 11 ..
4.125.d:
तथैव देवकी माता ज्ञानिनां च गुरोर्गुरोः ।
वसुदेववचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य शंकरः स्वयम्
चतुर्णामपि वेदानामुवाच जनको गुरुः ॥ 11 ॥
4.125.m: and likewise Devakī is the mother of the guru of the gurus of the wise.” / Hearing Vasudeva's words, Śaṅkara himself smiled, and the father and teacher of the four Vedas spoke.

4.125.s:
mahādeva uvāca
saṃnikarṣo jñānināṃ cāpyanādaraṇakāraṇam .
yānti gaṅgāmbhasā pūtāstīrthānyanyāni siddhaye .. 12 ..
4.125.d:
महादेव उवाच
संनिकर्षो ज्ञानिनां चाप्यनादरणकारणम् ।
यान्ति गङ्गाम्भसा पूतास्तीर्थान्यन्यानि सिद्धये ॥ 12 ॥
4.125.m:
Mahādeva said:
Even for the wise, close proximity is a cause of neglect: / purified by the waters of the Gaṅgā, people go to other holy places for spiritual perfection.

4.125.s:
vāsudevāsya tāto'yaṃ vasudevaśca paṇḍitaḥ .
jñāninaḥ kaśyapasyāśo vasostātasya cā''tmanaḥ .. 13 ..
4.125.d:
वासुदेवास्य तातोऽयं वसुदेवश्च पण्डितः ।
ज्ञानिनः कश्यपस्याशो वसोस्तातस्य चा'ऽत्मनः ॥ 13 ॥
4.125.m: This learned Vasudeva is the father of Vāsudeva, / a portion of the wise Kaśyapa, of the Vasu, and of his own father.

4.125.s:
pṛcchati jñānamasmāṃśca kṛṣṇājñānputrabuddhitaḥ .
aho durgā mahāmāyā jñānināmapi mohinī .. 14 ..
4.125.d:
पृच्छति ज्ञानमस्मांश्च कृष्णाज्ञान्पुत्रबुद्धितः ।
अहो दुर्गा महामाया ज्ञानिनामपि मोहिनी ॥ 14 ॥
4.125.m: He asks us for knowledge, thinking Kṛṣṇa to be merely his son. / Ah, Durgā, the great illusion, bewilders even the wise!

4.125.s:
viṣṇumāyā durārādhyā na sādhyā jāgatāmapi .
vayaṃ ca mohitāḥ śaśvadvedānāṃ janakastathā .. 15 ..
4.125.d:
विष्णुमाया दुराराध्या न साध्या जागतामपि ।
वयं च मोहिताः शश्वद्वेदानां जनकस्तथा ॥ 15 ॥
4.125.m: Viṣṇu's illusion is hard to propitiate, unattainable even by the world; / and we are constantly bewildered [by it], as is the father of the Vedas.

4.125.s:
brahmā kṛṣṇaṃ parīkṣeta mohitastasya māyayā .
dhyāyate yatpadāmbhojaṃ tapasā jīvanāvadhi .. 16 ..
4.125.d:
ब्रह्मा कृष्णं परीक्षेत मोहितस्तस्य मायया ।
ध्यायते यत्पदाम्भोजं तपसा जीवनावधि ॥ 16 ॥
4.125.m: Brahmā tests Kṛṣṇa, bewildered by his illusion— / [Kṛṣṇa] whose lotus feet he meditates upon through austerities for the duration of his life.

4.125.s:
indreṣu daśalakṣeṣvapyadhikāṣṭaśateṣu ca .
pāteṣu brahmaṇaḥ pāte nimeṣo mādhavasya ca .. 17 ..
4.125.d:
इन्द्रेषु दशलक्षेष्वप्यधिकाष्टशतेषु च ।
पातेषु ब्रह्मणः पाते निमेषो माधवस्य च ॥ 17 ॥
4.125.m: When ten hundred thousand and eight hundred more Indras / fall, and Brahmā falls, that is a mere blink of an eye for Mādhava.

4.125.s:
saha tenendrayuddhaṃ ca pārijātasya hetunā .
pārijātataruṃ dattvā mayā śakraśca rakṣitaḥ .. 18 ..
4.125.d:
सह तेनेन्द्रयुद्धं च पारिजातस्य हेतुना ।
पारिजाततरुं दत्त्वा मया शक्रश्च रक्षितः ॥ 18 ॥
4.125.m: There was a battle with Indra for the sake of the pārijāta tree; / by giving the pārijāta tree, Indra was protected by me.

4.125.s:
yajjñānaṃ na girāmeva tatvaṃ vā viṣayātmakam .
nahi kiṃ cittadajñānāṃ tasmāddhyānaṃ sadaiva hi .. 19 ..
4.125.d:
यज्ज्ञानं न गिरामेव तत्वं वा विषयात्मकम् ।
नहि किं चित्तदज्ञानां तस्माद्ध्यानं सदैव हि ॥ 19 ॥
4.125.m: That knowledge which is not accessible to speech or that reality consists of worldly sense-objects; / it is nothing to the ignorant, therefore meditation is indeed always [practised].

4.125.s:
prāṇināmātmano jñānamasmākaṃ jñānamasti ca .
tadūdharvaṃ tatsamaṃ naiva kṛṣṇaṃ pṛccha śubhāśumam .. 20 ..
4.125.d:
प्राणिनामात्मनो ज्ञानमस्माकं ज्ञानमस्ति च ।
तदूधर्वं तत्समं नैव कृष्णं पृच्छ शुभाशुमम् ॥ 20 ॥
4.125.m: Living beings have knowledge of the self, and we possess knowledge; / there is none above it and none equal to it; ask Kṛṣṇa about good and evil.

4.125.s:
brahmaṇaśca caturyāmaṃ kalpaṃ kalpavido viduḥ .
saptakalpāntajīvī ca mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ .. 21 ..
4.125.d:
ब्रह्मणश्च चतुर्यामं कल्पं कल्पविदो विदुः ।
सप्तकल्पान्तजीवी च मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ॥ 21 ॥
4.125.m: Those who know the kalpas know that four yāmas of Brahmā make a kalpa. / And the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya lives to the end of seven kalpas.

4.125.s:
aṣṭānavatiśakreṣu pāteṣu patanaṃ muneḥ .
tataḥ prāptaṃ harerdāsyaṃ muninā tapasaḥ phalāt .. 22 ..
4.125.d:
अष्टानवतिशक्रेषु पातेषु पतनं मुनेः ।
ततः प्राप्तं हरेर्दास्यं मुनिना तपसः फलात् ॥ 22 ॥
4.125.m: Upon the fall of ninety-eight Indras occurs the sage's fall; / thereafter, servitude to Hari was attained by the sage as the fruit of his austerities.

4.125.s:
pralaye brahmaṇaḥ pāte patanaṃ lomaśasya ca .
dikpālānāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca tadāyuścirajīvinām .. 23 ..
4.125.d:
प्रलये ब्रह्मणः पाते पतनं लोमशस्य च ।
दिक्पालानां ग्रहाणां च तदायुश्चिरजीविनाम् ॥ 23 ॥
4.125.m: In the dissolution, at the fall of Brahmā, occurs the fall of Lomaśa. / Such is the lifespan of the guardians of the directions, the planets, and the long-lived.

4.125.s:
anyeṣāmapi devānāṃ munīnāmūrdhvaretasām .
tadevā''yuśca rudrāṇāṃ māṃ ca mṛtyuṃjayaṃ vinā .. 24 ..
4.125.d:
अन्येषामपि देवानां मुनीनामूर्ध्वरेतसाम् ।
तदेवा'ऽयुश्च रुद्राणां मां च मृत्युंजयं विना ॥ 24 ॥
4.125.m: Such is also the lifespan of other gods, of sages whose seed is drawn up, / and of the Rudras, except for me, the conqueror of death.

4.125.s:
pralaye ca vidheḥ pāte śivaloke'pyahaṃ śivaḥ .
brahmabhālodbhavaḥ śaṃbhūḥ sarvādiḥ sargabhāṣaṇaḥ .. 25 ..
4.125.d:
प्रलये च विधेः पाते शिवलोकेऽप्यहं शिवः ।
ब्रह्मभालोद्भवः शंभूः सर्वादिः सर्गभाषणः ॥ 25 ॥
4.125.m: And in the dissolution, at the fall of the Creator, in the world of Śiva I am Śiva. / Born from the forehead of Brahmā, Śambhu is the beginning of all, the declarer of creation.

4.125.s:
kṛṣṇavāmāṅgasaṃbhūtā yathā rādhā tathaiva ca .
tathaiva durgā lakṣmīśca sāvitrī ca sarasvatī .. 26 ..
4.125.d:
कृष्णवामाङ्गसंभूता यथा राधा तथैव च ।
तथैव दुर्गा लक्ष्मीश्च सावित्री च सरस्वती ॥ 26 ॥
4.125.m: Just as Rādhā was born from the left side of Kṛṣṇa, / so too were Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sāvitrī, and Sarasvatī.

4.125.s:
ādityo''yaditeḥ putraḥ kāyavyūhena dvādaśa .
tathaiva ca mahendraśca kāyavyūhāccartudaśa .. 27 ..
4.125.d:
आदित्यो'ऽयदितेः पुत्रः कायव्यूहेन द्वादश ।
तथैव च महेन्द्रश्च कायव्यूहाच्चर्तुदश ॥ 27 ॥
4.125.m: The Āditya, the son of Aditi, became twelve through an array of bodies; / likewise Mahendra became fourteen through an array of bodies.

4.125.s:
tathaiva vasavaścāṣṭau rudrāścaikāvaśaiva te .
manupāte cendrapāto viṣayātpatanaṃ bhavet .. 28 ..
4.125.d:
तथैव वसवश्चाष्टौ रुद्राश्चैकावशैव ते ।
मनुपाते चेन्द्रपातो विषयात्पतनं भवेत् ॥ 28 ॥
4.125.m: Likewise the eight Vasus and the eleven Rudras. / At the fall of a Manu occurs the fall of an Indra; it is a fall from power over the realm.

4.125.s:
samāyayau ca sarveṣāṃ nidhanaṃ pralaye'pi ca .
pralayo darśayāmāsa brahmāṇḍaṃ ca jalaplutam .. 29 ..
4.125.d:
समाययौ च सर्वेषां निधनं प्रलयेऽपि च ।
प्रलयो दर्शयामास ब्रह्माण्डं च जलप्लुतम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.125.m: And the destruction of all arrived in the dissolution as well; / the dissolution revealed the cosmic egg inundated with water,

4.125.s:
brahmāṇaṃ ca svalokaṃ ca svātmānaṃ śaktibhiśca mām .
sarveṣāṃ mūlarūpaśca sarveśaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca .. 30 ..
4.125.d:
ब्रह्माणं च स्वलोकं च स्वात्मानं शक्तिभिश्च माम् ।
सर्वेषां मूलरूपश्च सर्वेशः कृष्ण एव च ॥ 30 ॥
4.125.m: and Brahmā, and his own realm, and myself together with my powers. / Kṛṣṇa alone is the original form of all, the lord of all.

4.125.s:
bhaja putraṃ rājasūye yajñeśaṃ yajñakāraṇam .
vidhivaddakṣiṇāṃ dattvāṃ bhavābdhiṃ tara yādava .. 31 ..
4.125.d:
भज पुत्रं राजसूये यज्ञेशं यज्ञकारणम् ।
विधिवद्दक्षिणां दत्त्वां भवाब्धिं तर यादव ॥ 31 ॥
4.125.m: Worship your son in the Rājasūya sacrifice, the lord of sacrifice, the cause of sacrifice; / having given the sacrificial fee according to rule, cross over the ocean of worldly existence, O Yādava!

4.125.s:
muktiste nāsti nirvāṇā viṣayī kaśyapo bhavāna .
na te dāsyaṃ ktadhanamaditirdevakī tathā .. 32 ..
4.125.d:
मुक्तिस्ते नास्ति निर्वाणा विषयी कश्यपो भवान ।
न ते दास्यं क्तधनमदितिर्देवकी तथा ॥ 32 ॥
4.125.m: You do not have ultimate liberation, [for] you are the worldly Kaśyapa; / you do not have servitude [to him], nor the wealth earned [thereby]; so also is Aditi, [who is] Devakī.

4.125.s:
vraja svargaṃ bhogabījaṃ svasthānamamarālayam .
śivasya vacanaṃ śrutvā saṃyata ścaśubhakṣaṇe .. 33 ..
4.125.d:
व्रज स्वर्गं भोगबीजं स्वस्थानममरालयम् ।
शिवस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा संयत श्चशुभक्षणे ॥ 33 ॥
4.125.m: Go to heaven, the source of enjoyment, your own abode, the dwelling of the immortals!" / Having heard Śiva's words, restrained, at an auspicious moment,

4.125.s:
tatra saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro rājasūyaṃ cakāra saḥ .
vasudevasya havyaṃ ca sākṣācca jagṛhaḥ surāḥ .. 34 ..
4.125.d:
तत्र संभृतसंभारो राजसूयं चकार सः ।
वसुदेवस्य हव्यं च साक्षाच्च जगृहः सुराः ॥ 34 ॥
4.125.m: having gathered the provisions there, he performed the Rājasūya sacrifice. / And the gods directly received the sacrificial offering of Vasudeva,

4.125.s:
yatra sākṣācca yajñeśo yajño'yaṃ dakṣiṇā saha .
būrṇāhutiṃ dattavantaṃ vasudevamuvāca saḥ ..
sanatkumāro bhagavānvāsudevājñayā mune .. 35 ..
4.125.d:
यत्र साक्षाच्च यज्ञेशो यज्ञोऽयं दक्षिणा सह ।
बूर्णाहुतिं दत्तवन्तं वसुदेवमुवाच सः ॥
सनत्कुमारो भगवान्वासुदेवाज्ञया मुने ॥ 35 ॥
4.125.m:
where the lord of sacrifice was present in person, this sacrifice along with the sacrificial fee. / To Vasudeva, who had offered the final oblations, he spoke—
the blessed Sanatkumāra, by the order of Vāsudeva, O sage:

4.125.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
sarvasvaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dehi turṇaṃ lakṣmīpateḥ pitaḥ .
sārthakaṃ kuru karmedaṃ vedoktaṃ vacanaṃ śruṇu .. 36 ..
4.125.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
सर्वस्वं दक्षिणां देहि तुर्णं लक्ष्मीपतेः पितः ।
सार्थकं कुरु कर्मेदं वेदोक्तं वचनं श्रुणु ॥ 36 ॥
4.125.m: Sanatkumāra said: / "Give all your possessions as the sacrificial fee quickly, O father of Lakṣmī's lord! / Make this rite fruitful; listen to the word declared in the Vedas:

4.125.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ vipramuddiśya tatkālaṃ cenna dīyate .
muhūrte tu vyatīte sā dakṣiṇā dviguṇā bhavet .. 37 ..
4.125.d:
दक्षिणां विप्रमुद्दिश्य तत्कालं चेन्न दीयते ।
मुहूर्ते तु व्यतीते सा दक्षिणा द्विगुणा भवेत् ॥ 37 ॥
4.125.m: If a sacrificial fee intended for a brahmin is not given at that very time, / when a muhūrta has passed, that sacrificial fee becomes double.

4.125.s:
vāsare ca bahirbhūte bhavetsā'pi caturguṇā .
trirātre samatīte ṣaḍguṇā dakṣiṇā bhavet .. 38 ..
4.125.d:
वासरे च बहिर्भूते भवेत्साऽपि चतुर्गुणा ।
त्रिरात्रे समतीते षड्गुणा दक्षिणा भवेत् ॥ 38 ॥
4.125.m: When a day has passed away, it becomes fourfold; / when three nights have elapsed, the sacrificial fee becomes sixfold.

4.125.s:
pakṣānte tu śataguṇā māsānte tu caturguṇā .
ṣaṇmāse'pyadhike nyūne ca sāhastraguṇā tathā .. 39 ..
4.125.d:
पक्षान्ते तु शतगुणा मासान्ते तु चतुर्गुणा ।
षण्मासेऽप्यधिके न्यूने च साहस्त्रगुणा तथा ॥ 39 ॥
4.125.m: At the end of a fortnight it is a hundredfold, and at the end of a month four[fold]; / whether a little more or less than six months, likewise a thousandfold.

4.125.s:
varṣānte sā lakṣaguṇā brahmaṇoktaṃ ca yāṭava .
ubhau ca narakaṃ yāṃtaḥ karmakartṛpurohitau .. 40 ..
4.125.d:
वर्षान्ते सा लक्षगुणा ब्रह्मणोक्तं च याटव ।
उभौ च नरकं यांतः कर्मकर्तृपुरोहितौ ॥ 40 ॥
4.125.m: At the end of a year it is a hundred thousandfold; this has been spoken by Brahmā, O Yādava. / And both go to hell—the performer of the rite and the family priest."

4.125.s:
vāsudaivaśca tacchutvā sarvasvamutsasarjaṃ saḥ .
adhikārāṃśca sāh lādo vāsudevājñayā tathā .. 41 ..
4.125.d:
वासुदैवश्च तच्छुत्वा सर्वस्वमुत्ससर्जं सः ।
अधिकारांश्च साह् लादो वासुदेवाज्ञया तथा ॥ 41 ॥
4.125.m: And Vasudeva, having heard that, renounced all his possessions / and his rights, with great joy, by the command of Vāsudeva.

4.125.s:
amūlyānāṃ ca ratnānāṃ daśakoṭimanuttamamā .
dadau gargāya sarvādau svayaṃ lakṣmaupateḥ pitā .. 42 ..
4.125.d:
अमूल्यानां च रत्नानां दशकोटिमनुत्तममा ।
ददौ गर्गाय सर्वादौ स्वयं लक्ष्मौपतेः पिता ॥ 42 ॥
4.125.m: A hundred million priceless and incomparable gems / he himself gave first of all to Garga, the father of Lakṣmī's lord—

4.125.s:
śatakoṭiṃ maṇīndrāṇāṃ svarṇānāṃ taccartuguṇam .
māṇikyānāṃ ca muktānāṃ hīrakāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 43 ..
4.125.d:
शतकोटिं मणीन्द्राणां स्वर्णानां तच्चर्तुगुणम् ।
माणिक्यानां च मुक्तानां हीरकाणां तथैव च ॥ 43 ॥
4.125.m: a thousand million best jewels, four times as much gold, / and of rubies, pearls, and likewise diamonds;

4.125.s:
raupyaṃ pravālaṃ paramaṃ svarṇapātrāṇi yāni ca .
svastrīṇāṃ svavadhūnāṃ cāpyamūlyaratnabhūṣaṇam .. 44 ..
4.125.d:
रौप्यं प्रवालं परमं स्वर्णपात्राणि यानि च ।
स्वस्त्रीणां स्ववधूनां चाप्यमूल्यरत्नभूषणम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.125.m: silver, excellent coral, whatever golden vessels there were, / and the priceless jewelled ornaments of his women and daughters-in-law;

4.125.s:
śvetacāmaralakṣaṃ ca lakṣaṃ ca ratnadarpaṇam .
kāmadhenugaṇaṃ sarvaṃ śatakoṭiṃ gajānapi .. 45 ..
4.125.d:
श्वेतचामरलक्षं च लक्षं च रत्नदर्पणम् ।
कामधेनुगणं सर्वं शतकोटिं गजानपि ॥ 45 ॥
4.125.m: a hundred thousand white fly-whisks, and a hundred thousand jewelled mirrors, / all herds of wish-fulfilling cows, and also a thousand million elephants;

4.125.s:
śatakauṭiṃ gajendrāṇāmaśvānāṃ taccaturguṇam .
yaddhanaṃ yādavānāṃ ca rājño rājanumodanāt .. 46 ..
4.125.d:
शतकौटिं गजेन्द्राणामश्वानां तच्चतुर्गुणम् ।
यद्धनं यादवानां च राज्ञो राजनुमोदनात् ॥ 46 ॥
4.125.m: a thousand million lordly elephants, and four times as many horses, / whatever wealth belonged to the Yādavas, with the approval of the king, O king;

4.125.s:
grāmāṇāṃ śatalakṣaṃ ca sasasyaṃ phalitaṃ tarum .
dhānyācalānāṃ lakṣaṃ ca śālyannānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 47 ..
4.125.d:
ग्रामाणां शतलक्षं च ससस्यं फलितं तरुम् ।
धान्याचलानां लक्षं च शाल्यन्नानां तथैव च ॥ 47 ॥
